Employees must be free of illegal drugs and alcohol while on duty and free of legal substances that impair their duties. The employee handbook states this and each employee signs an acknowledgment at hire and each year (COC-02).

An employee taking a prescription or over-the-counter medication that may cause drowsiness or impair judgment must tell the supervisor before the shift if it could affect safe work, without having to name the medication or condition. The supervisor decides with the employee whether duties need to be changed or the employee needs to be relieved.

If a supervisor reasonably suspects impairment (for example slurred speech, odor of alcohol, unsteady movement or unusual behavior), the supervisor, with another manager as witness where possible, speaks to the employee, records the observations and removes the employee from resident contact. The employee does not drive and is given a safe ride home. The Administrator is notified at once.

The Administrator follows [AGENCY NAME]'s written drug and alcohol testing procedure for reasonable suspicion and uses a certified collection site. A refusal to test or a positive test is handled under COC-02 and STF-07 and may lead to discipline up to termination. Where the employee is a licensed professional, the Administrator makes any report to the licensing board that the law requires.

Employees with symptoms of a contagious illness such as vomiting, diarrhea, fever, a new rash, or an open skin lesion that cannot be covered, tell the supervisor and do not work with residents until they are free of symptoms for the period the nurse specifies (INF-01). The Administrator arranges coverage so that no shift is left short (STF-01).

The Administrator reviews the health file of each employee at least once a year and at each new hire to confirm TB screening is complete, hepatitis B vaccination status or declination is on file and bloodborne pathogen training is current.
Employee health results and information about impairment are reported to QI only in summary form, with no identifiers, as part of infection control and risk indicators (QA-01).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures all employees complete TB screening, vaccination offers, bloodborne pathogen training and fitness-for-duty acknowledgments, and keeps health files secure.
Reviews TB risk assessments and results, directs follow-up after exposure, coordinates with the health department and advises on work restrictions.
Observe for impairment and illness, remove employees from duty when needed and notify the Administrator.
Complete screening, report symptoms, exposures and impairing medications, and come to work fit for duty.

documentation: TB risk assessment, symptom evaluation and test results (personnel file)
Records of repeat screening after known exposure
Medical clearance for any positive test or symptoms
Hepatitis B vaccination record or signed declination
Annual bloodborne pathogen training record
Exposure incident reports and follow-up
Signed drug and alcohol acknowledgment
Reasonable-suspicion observation records and testing results (confidential file)

policies.category: Staffing, staff training and credential verification
policies.title: Personnel Records
policies.applies_to: All employees and contractors who work with residents; the Administrator; the human resources designee
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] keeps a complete, current and retrievable personnel file for every person who works with residents. The file is how the agency shows that staff were screened, trained and found competent before they worked alone.
policies.policy: This policy meets 82-13-1-.05(8)(j) (proposed), 'What constitutes the staffing requirements and how the residence will ensure that staff are trained, including but not limited to the following required elements.' It does so by setting out the personnel file contents that prove staff are screened, trained and competent. STF-01 sets staffing levels and STF-04 sets orientation and training content. [AGENCY NAME] keeps a personnel file for every employee. Each file contains: (1) an eligible criminal background determination; (2) a motor vehicle record (MVR) check; (3) TB screening on hire, which is a risk assessment, symptom evaluation and test, repeated on known exposure; (4) first aid and BCLS training with recertification; (5) evidence of training and competency, including 16 hours of continuing education each year; (6) the signed code of conduct acknowledgment, renewed every year; (7) the job description; and (8) the annual performance evaluation. The file also holds the registry check, the records check application, the verified five-year employment history and proof of age. The Administrator must be at least 21 years old and all other employees at least 18. No employee works alone with residents until all minimum training and documented competence are complete. Personnel files are kept at the home or are readily available to a surveyor during an unannounced survey. [AGENCY NAME] follows the Fair Labor Standards Act as it applies to domestic service employment (29 CFR Part 552) and keeps the payroll and timekeeping records needed to show compliance.

definitions.definition: The confidential record kept for each employee or contractor who works with residents. It holds the screening, training, competency, evaluation and conduct documents listed in this policy.
The documented result of the criminal background check showing the person is eligible to work with residents under Georgia law and DBHDD requirements.
Motor vehicle record, obtained for each employee. It is reviewed for any employee who may transport residents (see ENV-02).
Basic cardiac life support. This is CPR and related emergency skills at a level that meets the certifying body's current standard.
Documented observation or testing by a qualified trainer that the employee can perform a task correctly, as distinct from attending a class.

procedures: Before the first day of work, the Administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) or a designee opens a personnel file and a personnel file checklist for each new employee. No one is placed on the schedule until the pre-hire items on the checklist are complete.
The Administrator confirms and files proof that the employee is at least 18 years old (the Administrator must be at least 21).

Before employment, the designee completes and files the registry check, the records check application and the criminal background check (O.C.G.A. 37-1-141 and 37-1-143). The Administrator reviews the result and signs the eligibility determination. STF-03 describes this process. A person without an eligible determination is not hired.

The Administrator verifies the employee's five-year employment history by contacting prior employers or other sources. The Administrator records the date, source and result on the file checklist and initials it.
The designee obtains and files an MVR for each employee. The Administrator reviews it before the employee is assigned any driving duty.

On hire, the employee completes the TB risk assessment and symptom evaluation and has a TB test. The nurse or health professional reviews the results, and the results are filed in the confidential health section of the file (STF-05). After any known TB exposure, the screening is repeated and the new result is filed.

The employee provides first aid and BCLS certificates. The designee files them and enters the expiration dates in the training tracker. The Administrator confirms that at least one employee currently trained in BCLS and first aid is on duty every shift.
Before any direct contact with residents, the employee completes orientation (see STF-04). The trainer signs the orientation record and the signed record goes in the file.

The trainer or supervisor documents training and competency as it is completed. The employee must finish the full required training list within 60 days of hire. Each year the employee must complete at least 16 hours of training or continuing education and have competency validated. Certificates, sign-in sheets and competency checklists are filed with dates and the trainer's name.
At hire and every year, the employee signs the code of conduct acknowledgment (COC-01 and COC-02). The Administrator files the signed copy. An employee who has not signed is not scheduled.

At hire, the employee signs the job description. The employee also signs a statement that he or she will be free of illegal drugs and alcohol, and of any legal substance that impairs job duties, while working (STF-05).
The supervisor completes a written performance evaluation of each employee every year, reviews it with the employee, and files it signed by both. Findings feed the employee's training plan.

The designee reviews the tracker monthly and flags any certificate, TB item, evaluation, code-of-conduct renewal or training hours that will expire or fall due within 30 days. The Administrator makes sure the item is fixed before it lapses.

If a required item lapses, the Administrator removes the employee from the affected duty (for example, driving or being the only BCLS-certified staff on a shift). The Administrator does not let the employee work alone with residents until the item is current, and documents the action in the file.
The Administrator audits every file against the checklist at hire and then at least quarterly. The audit is dated and signed, and any gaps are corrected with a documented due date.

The designee keeps personnel files in a locked cabinet or access-controlled electronic system at the home or where they can be produced immediately. Files must be available for unannounced surveys. The Administrator gives DBHDD staff and other authorized reviewers prompt access.
Supervisors review and sign employee timesheets. The designee keeps payroll and timekeeping records that show compliance with the Fair Labor Standards Act (29 CFR Part 552).
The designee files in the personnel file any corrective or disciplinary action (STF-07). Files of former employees are kept as required by REC-01.

responsibilities.duty: Approves this policy, makes sure resources exist to maintain personnel files, and reviews audit results.
Verifies employment history, signs eligibility determinations, audits files quarterly, and removes employees from duties when items lapse.
Builds and maintains files, runs the expiration tracker, and secures records.
Document competency, complete evaluations and sign timesheets.
Provide accurate documents, keep certifications current and sign required acknowledgments.

documentation: Personnel file and checklist for each employee
Criminal background eligibility determination, registry check and records check application
MVR
TB screening records, kept in the confidential health section
First aid and BCLS certificates
Orientation, training, competency and annual 16-hour continuing education records
Signed code of conduct acknowledgments, renewed annually
Job description and drug/alcohol-free statement
Annual performance evaluations
Verified five-year employment history
Expiration tracker and quarterly audit forms
Timesheets and payroll records

policies.category: Staffing, staff training and credential verification
policies.title: Staff Conduct Inconsistent with Policy and Professional Boundaries
policies.applies_to: All employees, contractors, volunteers and governing body members; the Administrator
policies.purpose: To set out how [AGENCY NAME] responds when a staff member acts in a way that conflicts with agency policy. It also sets professional boundaries that protect residents from exploitation and from conflicts of interest.
policies.policy: This policy meets 290-9-37-.07(3)(l) (how the residence handles acts committed by staff or residents that are inconsistent with policies of the residence) for staff conduct, and 82-13-1-.05(8)(j)4 (proposed) (how the residence handles acts committed by staff that are inconsistent with policies of the residence). RAC-01 covers resident conduct. [AGENCY NAME] follows its written policies, as C4 requires. Any act by a staff member that conflicts with a written policy is reported, assessed, investigated when needed, and met with corrective or disciplinary action that is documented in the personnel file. Conduct that may be abuse, neglect or exploitation is handled under ABE-01 and ABE-02 first, and resident safety comes before any personnel process. No governing body member, staff member or family member of staff may serve as a resident's representative or guardian. No one may solicit a resident to name staff as a beneficiary of a will, trust or life insurance policy. No life insurance may be taken out on a resident. Gifts from residents are investigated. An involuntary gift is reported to law enforcement and to the resident's legal representative. Staff may not use the home as a personal residence.

definitions.definition: Any act or omission by a staff member that violates a written policy of [AGENCY NAME], the code of conduct, or a rule that applies to the home. It includes failing to report such conduct.
The limit that separates a staff member's professional role from personal, financial or social involvement with a resident that could cause harm or a conflict of interest.
Money, property, services, or a benefit of any kind given by a resident or the resident's family to a staff member, including a bequest or a beneficiary designation.
A gift obtained through pressure, solicitation, deception or a resident's inability to understand what is being given.

procedures: Orientation and annual training cover this policy. Every employee signs the code of conduct each year (COC-01, COC-02), including the boundary rules in this policy.

Any employee who sees or learns of conduct that conflicts with policy reports it to the Administrator or the supervisor on duty immediately. If the conduct involves the Administrator, the report goes to the governing body chair [GOVERNING BODY CHAIR NAME]. Reports can be made verbally or in writing, and no one is punished for making a good-faith report (RGT-02).

If a resident may be at risk, the supervisor protects the resident immediately. This includes separating the staff member from the resident, calling 911 if needed, and securing the resident's safety and medical care.

If the report may involve abuse, neglect or exploitation, the Administrator follows ABE-01 and ABE-02, including notifications and reports to the state. Personnel action does not delay or replace those reports.
The Administrator opens a written conduct review the same day or the next business day. The review records who reported, what happened, when and where, who was involved, and the policy involved.
When the allegation is serious, the Administrator removes the staff member from duty or from resident contact while the review is open. The Administrator documents the reason and the date.

The Administrator interviews the staff member, the reporter and witnesses, reviews any records or other evidence, and writes a finding of substantiated, unsubstantiated or inconclusive. The Administrator finishes the review within [NUMBER] business days unless an outside agency needs more time.

For substantiated violations the Administrator selects a response based on the seriousness of the act, harm or risk to residents, and the staff member's history. Responses range from coaching with documentation, to retraining and competency re-validation, to a written warning, suspension, or termination. Any act of abuse, neglect, exploitation or theft is grounds for termination.

The Administrator meets with the staff member, explains the finding and the action, and gives the staff member the chance to respond in writing. The staff member signs to acknowledge receipt. A refusal to sign is noted.
The Administrator files the review, finding, action taken and any staff response in the personnel file (STF-06). The Administrator also records any retraining.

Professional boundaries: staff may not borrow money from, lend money to, or sell goods to residents. They may not use a resident's money, property, card or accounts for any personal purpose (RGT-03). They may not take on a financial or legal role for a resident, and may not engage in romantic or sexual contact with a resident. They may not give out their personal contact information or befriend residents on social media. They may not take photos or video of residents for personal use or post them (CONF-01).

No governing body member, staff member or staff family member may serve as a resident's representative or guardian. At admission and each annual ISP review, the case manager checks that no such person is named, and records the check. If a conflict is found, the Administrator tells the resident and the team, and the resident gets support to choose another representative (RGT-04).

No staff or governing body member may solicit or suggest that a resident name staff as a beneficiary of a will, trust or life insurance policy. Staff may not take out life insurance on a resident. Staff must report any such request or document they learn of to the Administrator immediately.

Staff report any gift offered or received from a resident or family to the Administrator on the same shift or the next business day. The Administrator investigates each gift, records the facts and the resident's wishes and understanding, and decides whether the item is returned. The investigation record goes into the Administrator's gift log.

If the Administrator finds a gift was involuntary, the Administrator reports it to local law enforcement and to the resident's legal representative or guardian the same day. The Administrator also considers whether ABE-01 applies, and records the report in the incident file.
Staff may not use the home as a personal residence. The Administrator checks this when assigning shifts and during the quarterly home audit.
The Administrator reviews all conduct reviews quarterly and gives the pattern to the QA committee for training and prevention actions (QA-01).

responsibilities.duty: Makes sure policies are followed, receives reports about the Administrator, and reviews summaries of conduct reviews.
Opens and completes conduct reviews, decides on corrective action, investigates gifts, and makes reports to law enforcement and legal representatives.
Protect residents on the spot and report conduct immediately.
Follow the code of conduct and boundary rules and report conduct that conflicts with policy.

documentation: Conduct review report with findings and action taken
Staff acknowledgment and any staff response
Corrective or disciplinary action in the personnel file
Gift log and gift investigation records
Law enforcement and legal representative notification records
Annual code of conduct acknowledgments
Representative and guardian conflict check at admission and each annual ISP review
QA quarterly summary of conduct reviews

policies.title: Levels of Observation and Supervision
policies.applies_to: All direct care staff, supervisors, nurse, ISP team members and the Administrator
policies.purpose: To make sure every resident is observed and supervised at the level that meets his or her clinical care and safety needs. The level must be the least restrictive that is safe and must be defined in writing.
policies.policy: This policy meets 82-13-1-.05(8)(k) (proposed), 'Levels of observation procedures to meet the residents' clinical care and safety needs.' [AGENCY NAME] assigns each resident an observation level based on assessed need, records it in the ISP, and tells all staff on duty. The levels are general supervision, periodic checks, 1:1 line-of-sight and 1:1 arm's-length. The program description (SCP-01) states the minimum staff-to-resident ratios and defines 1:1 arm's-length and line-of-sight staffing, as C33 requires. Staffing is always enough to protect health, safety and welfare and to evacuate all residents within three minutes. Staff are awake in the home at all times during their scheduled shift. If any resident will be in the home without staff, the ISP must first document an assessment of that resident's capacity to be independent. Observation is never used as punishment, and it respects the resident's rights (RGT-01).

definitions.definition: Staff are present and awake in the home, know where each resident is, and are available to help. Residents move freely within the home and community according to the ISP.
Staff physically check on or see the resident at set intervals written in the ISP, for example because of seizure risk, a health condition or a recent change.
One assigned staff member keeps the resident continuously in view and close enough to step in at once. The staff member has no other duties that take attention away.
One assigned staff member stays within arm's reach of the resident at all times, with privacy arrangements for toileting and bathing written in the ISP.
The documented assessment in the ISP of whether a resident can safely be in the home, or in the community, without staff for a stated period.
The written ISP entry that states the level, the reason, the start date, who may change it and when it is reviewed.

procedures: Before or at admission, the ISP team assesses each resident's clinical care and safety needs. These include health conditions, seizures, choking risk, fall risk, wandering and elopement risk, behavioral risk, medication needs and the resident's history. The team consists of the resident, the representative if any, the nurse, the case manager or QIDP, a behavior professional if one is involved, and direct care staff.

The team chooses the least restrictive observation level that meets the assessed needs and writes it in the ISP (PCS-01) with the reason, the start date, the staff responsible and the review date. The team gives the resident and representative the chance to agree or object, and records the response.

The Administrator posts, in a staff-only area, each resident's current observation level and any specific instruction. The Administrator updates the posting whenever the ISP changes. Staff may not post this information where visitors can see it (CONF-01).

The program description (SCP-01) states the minimum staff-to-resident ratio for day, evening and overnight shifts: [DAY RATIO], [EVENING RATIO], [OVERNIGHT RATIO]. The Administrator raises staffing above these ratios when any resident's observation level requires more staff.

The Administrator confirms that the ratio on every shift is sufficient to evacuate all residents within three minutes. This is tested during fire drills (EMG-03). If a drill takes longer than three minutes, the Administrator adds staff or changes the plan before the next shift.

Staff stay awake in the home throughout their shift, including overnight. A sleeping or absent staff member is a policy violation handled under STF-07. A supervisor on duty or on call is always reachable at [PHONE].

For 1:1 line-of-sight and arm's-length levels, the Administrator assigns a named staff member each shift and arranges breaks so the resident is never left uncovered. The assigned staff member hands off in person to the next staff member and records the handoff.

For periodic checks, staff record the time, location and condition of the resident on the observation log each time a check is done. A missed check is reported to the supervisor right away and documented.

No resident is left in the home without staff unless the ISP contains a current independence assessment. The assessment covers emergency response, medication, meals, use of the telephone, safety in the home and the length of time alone. The team re-assesses after any incident or change in condition.
Residents are not staff. No resident may be required to do staff tasks, including watching other residents, unless the ISP documents that the resident has chosen to take part voluntarily (RGT-01).
Staff follow the observation level for community outings and transportation (ENV-02) and report any change in the resident's behavior or health during an outing to the supervisor.

When a resident's risk increases, for example after a fall, seizure, behavior crisis, illness or elopement attempt, the supervisor may raise the observation level immediately to protect the resident. The supervisor tells the Administrator and the nurse the same day and records the change in the incident record (ABE-02). The ISP team meets within [NUMBER] business days to review and set the level.

The ISP team reviews each resident's observation level at least at every ISP review and after every incident or change in condition (HLT-03). A level is lowered only by team decision, written in the ISP with the reason.
If a restraint is used in a crisis, staff follow RST-01 and RST-02, including checks at least every 15 minutes. These checks are in addition to any observation level and do not replace it.

Observation does not limit rights. Staff knock before entering bedrooms, protect privacy for bathing and toileting to the extent safe, and do not read private mail. They do not deny visitors or phone access. Any limit needed for safety is written in the ISP with a reason and a plan to remove it (RGT-01).
The QA committee reviews observation levels, missed checks and related incidents at least quarterly (QA-01).

responsibilities.duty: Sets staffing to meet the ratios and observation levels, posts levels for staff, and reviews logs.
Assesses needs, chooses the level, documents the independence assessment and reviews levels.
Advises on health-related observation needs and reassesses after changes in condition.
Carry out the assigned level, complete logs and report missed checks or increased risk.
Assigns 1:1 staff, covers breaks, and may raise a level in an emergency.

documentation: Observation level order in the ISP with reason and review date
Independence assessment in the ISP
Observation logs for periodic checks and 1:1 handoffs
Staff-only posting of levels
Monthly coverage plan and record of actual coverage (STF-01)
Evacuation drill times (EMG-03)
Incident reports for missed checks or level changes
QA quarterly review of observation levels

policies.title: Resident Conduct Inconsistent with Home Policy
policies.applies_to: All staff, the Administrator, ISP team members, residents and representatives
policies.purpose: To set out how [AGENCY NAME] responds when a resident acts in a way that conflicts with the policies of the home. The response must be respectful, supportive and lawful, and must protect the resident's rights.
policies.policy: This policy meets 82-13-1-.05(8)(l) (proposed), how the residence handles acts committed by residents that are inconsistent with the policies of the residence, and 290-9-37-.07(3)(l) for the resident portion. STF-07 covers the staff portion of .07(3)(l). [AGENCY NAME] responds to resident conduct through positive behavior support, not punishment (RST-02). Staff look for the reason behind the behavior, address the unmet need, teach and encourage alternatives, and involve the resident and the ISP team. Chemical restraint, seclusion, restraint devices that are not medical support devices, and prone restraint are never used. Restraint is used only as a last resort in an emergency under RST-01. Staff may not infringe a resident's non-waivable rights as a consequence of conduct. These rights include visitors at agreed times, telephone access, private uncensored communication, bedroom privacy, control of property and money, personal needs allowance, choice of physician and access to records (RGT-01). Involuntary discharge follows the 30-day notice process in ADS-02. Immediate transfer is allowed only under the conditions listed there.

definitions.definition: A resident's act that conflicts with the written cooperative living expectations (ADS-05) or other home policy, such as endangering others, damaging property, or repeatedly disrupting the home.
A person-centered approach that identifies why a behavior occurs, changes the environment and supports, and teaches new skills to meet the same need.
A resident right that the home may not suspend, remove or make conditional on behavior, as described in RGT-01.
A written plan in the ISP or behavior support plan that tells staff how to respond to a specific crisis and when emergency help must be called.

procedures: At admission, the case manager explains the cooperative living expectations (ADS-05) to the resident and representative in plain language and in the resident's preferred communication method (RGT-05). The resident receives a written copy and any questions are recorded.

When a resident acts in a way that conflicts with policy, the staff member on duty stays calm, makes sure everyone is safe, and responds in a respectful way. Staff do not shame, threaten, argue with, ignore or punish the resident.

Staff first try to understand the cause. They check for pain, illness, medication effects, a change in routine, boredom, sensory overload, fear, or a communication problem. Staff use calming, redirecting and de-escalation techniques that the resident's plan and training allow.

If anyone is in immediate danger, staff call 911, protect the people involved and follow the resident's crisis or safety plan. Staff do not use the police or emergency services as a way to discipline a resident.
Staff record the behavior objectively in the daily notes: what happened before, what the resident did, how staff responded, and how it ended. Staff report to the supervisor by the end of the shift.

The supervisor reviews the report, decides whether it meets incident reporting criteria (ABE-02) and makes the report if so. If the behavior involved harm to another resident, the supervisor also follows ABE-01, since resident-to-resident harm may be abuse or neglect.

The supervisor tells the nurse if there may be a health cause and tells the representative or guardian. The Administrator arranges an ISP team meeting within [NUMBER] business days when behavior is repeated or serious.

The ISP team, including the resident, assesses the function of the behavior and updates the ISP with supports, teaching goals, environmental changes and the staff response. A behavior professional is involved if a positive behavior support plan is needed (RST-02).

Responses that are not allowed: removing visitors, phone access, mail, privacy, personal property, spending money, personal needs allowance, meals, medications, a choice of physician, or participation in care planning as a consequence. Staff also may not use seclusion, a locked room, or a threat of discharge to control behavior.

Natural, voluntary and reasonable responses are allowed. Examples are asking a resident to help repair something, talking through what happened, or a short, voluntary break in a quiet space. The resident must be free to leave at any time. Any financial responsibility for damage is decided only with the resident's and representative's informed consent and never taken from the personal needs allowance without that consent (RGT-03, RGT-04).

If crisis intervention becomes necessary, only staff with current nationally benchmarked crisis-intervention training may do it. Restraint is a last resort, must be in the ISP, behavior support plan or crisis plan, and is released when danger ends. Prone restraint is never used. Staff check the resident at least every 15 minutes, including pressure sites, and notify the representative or guardian by phone within 24 hours. Staff document the interventions tried and all checks (RST-01).

If a resident's conduct persists and the home can no longer meet the resident's needs or protect others, the Administrator convenes the ISP team and the Regional Field Office or support coordinator to look at additional supports and alternatives (ADM-01).

Discharge for conduct follows ADS-02. The Administrator gives at least 30 days' written notice, with the reason, the resident's right to complain and appeal, and help finding another placement. Expedited or immediate transfer is allowed only for the conditions defined in ADS-02, such as an immediate threat to health or safety. The Administrator documents the reason and any alternatives tried.
A resident or representative who disagrees with any response may file a complaint without fear of retaliation (RGT-02). Staff tell residents about this right.
The QA committee reviews behavior incidents, restraint use and discharges for conduct at least quarterly. The Rights Sub-Committee reviews each use of restrictive intervention (QA-01).

responsibilities.duty: Makes sure responses follow this policy, convenes the ISP team, and decides on any discharge according to ADS-02.
Assesses the reasons for behavior and builds supports into the ISP.
Develops and reviews positive behavior support plans where needed.
Respond respectfully, use de-escalation, document and report.
Reviews reports, makes incident reports, and notifies the representative and the nurse.

documentation: Written cooperative living expectations given to each resident
Daily note and behavior record
Incident reports where criteria are met
ISP and behavior support plan updates
Notification to representative or guardian within 24 hours when restraint is used
Restraint documentation and 15-minute check records
30-day discharge notice and any immediate transfer documentation
Resident complaint records
QA and Rights Sub-Committee review minutes

policies.title: Infection and Infestation Control
policies.applies_to: All staff, the nurse, the Administrator, residents and visitors
policies.purpose: To prevent and control infections and infestations in the home, protecting residents, staff and visitors, while respecting each resident's rights and home-like setting.
policies.policy: This policy meets 82-13-1-.05(8)(m) (proposed), 'Procedures for controlling and preventing infections and infestations in the residence.' [AGENCY NAME] uses standard precautions for all residents at all times. The agency has a written bloodborne pathogen exposure control plan and supplies personal protective equipment (PPE) at no cost to staff, as required by 29 CFR 1910.1030. Staff are screened for TB on hire, and again after a known exposure (risk assessment, symptom evaluation and test) as C8 requires. Infection control is a monitored risk area in the quality improvement program, reviewed at least quarterly (C35, QA-01). Staff are trained at orientation and annually. Infection precautions never include seclusion and never override a resident's rights.

definitions.definition: Basic infection prevention practices applied to all residents regardless of diagnosis: hand hygiene, PPE, safe handling of sharps, cleaning and waste handling.
The presence of parasites or pests such as lice, scabies, bed bugs, fleas or insects and rodents in the home or on a person.
A specific contact with blood or other potentially infectious material through the eye, mouth, other mucous membrane, non-intact skin, or a puncture, during duties.
Two or more residents or staff with the same illness, or an unusual increase in infection, in a short time in the home.
Personal protective equipment such as gloves, gowns, masks and eye protection.

procedures: The Administrator designates an infection control lead ([NURSE OR DESIGNEE NAME]) who oversees this policy, keeps supplies stocked and reports to the Administrator.

Before any employee works with residents, the employee completes the TB risk assessment, symptom evaluation and test, and the results are filed in the personnel file (STF-05, STF-06). After a known exposure to TB, the employee is re-screened right away and the result is filed. Staff with symptoms stay out of the home and are cleared before they return.

Staff wash hands with soap and water, or alcohol-based rub when hands are not visibly soiled, before and after resident care, before preparing or serving food, before and after medication passes, after toileting or using gloves, and after cleaning. Soap, paper towels and hand rub are available in each bathroom, the kitchen and the medication area.

Staff wear disposable gloves when touching blood, body fluids, broken skin, or soiled items, and add gowns, masks or eye protection when splashes are possible. Staff remove PPE properly and discard it in the right container. The agency supplies PPE in the sizes needed at no cost to staff.

The agency keeps a written bloodborne pathogen exposure control plan, reviewed at least annually. It identifies tasks with exposure risk and offers the hepatitis B vaccination series, at no cost, to employees with occupational exposure within 10 working days of assignment, as 29 CFR 1910.1030 provides. Staff may decline in writing.

Sharps, such as lancets and needles, go into puncture-resistant containers that are labeled and kept out of resident reach. Staff never recap, bend or break needles. Full containers are disposed of as medical waste according to MED-04 and local requirements.

After an exposure incident, the employee washes the area right away and reports to the supervisor. The Administrator arranges a confidential medical evaluation and follow-up at no cost, documents the circumstances, and files a written incident report (ABE-02). Medical records of the evaluation are kept confidential.

Staff clean and disinfect high-touch surfaces (doorknobs, switches, handrails, faucets, bathrooms, kitchen counters) at least daily, and immediately after soiling with an EPA-registered disinfectant used as the label directs. Staff clean blood and body-fluid spills at once using PPE and disinfectant.

Laundry soiled with body fluids is handled with gloves, bagged where it is soiled, and washed with detergent at the hottest temperature the fabric allows. Staff do not carry soiled laundry against the body.
Food safety follows HLT-04: handwashing, no food handling by anyone with vomiting, diarrhea or open infected sores, correct storage temperatures, and food discarded after its use-by date.

Staff offer residents help with hand hygiene, vaccines recommended by their physician, and routine health care. Staff tell the nurse when a resident shows symptoms such as fever, cough, vomiting, diarrhea, rash, itching or open sores.

When a resident is ill, the nurse is notified and the resident's physician is contacted (HLT-03). With the resident's agreement and on clinical advice, the resident may rest in his or her own room, and staff provide meals, care and company there. A resident is never locked in or kept in seclusion.

For suspected lice, scabies, bed bugs or other infestations, the nurse arranges evaluation and treatment by the resident's physician. Staff launder or bag linens and clothing, treat the room and shared furniture as directed, and arrange professional pest control when needed. Staff protect the resident's dignity and privacy and do not discard personal belongings without the resident's consent.

When an outbreak is suspected, the Administrator notifies the local public health authority as required by law, follows its instructions, increases cleaning and hand hygiene, and informs representatives and guardians. Any required report to the state follows ABE-02 and REC-02.

Staff tell visitors to stay away if they are ill. Visitors are not turned away from the home without cause, and any visit restriction is limited, temporary and consistent with RGT-01 and public health direction.
At orientation and every year, the nurse trains staff on standard precautions, PPE, bloodborne pathogens and the infestation response, and documents competency (STF-04).
The infection control lead keeps a log of infections, exposures and infestations. The QA committee reviews it at least quarterly, looks for patterns, and records corrective actions (QA-01).

responsibilities.duty: Keeps supplies and an exposure control plan, arranges post-exposure care, and notifies public health when needed.
Trains staff, advises on illness and infestation, keeps the infection log and updates the plan annually.
Practice standard precautions, wear PPE, clean the home and report symptoms and exposures right away.
Reviews infection data quarterly and tracks improvements.

documentation: TB screening and re-screening records in personnel files
Bloodborne pathogen exposure control plan and annual review
Hepatitis B vaccination offer or declination
Exposure incident reports and medical follow-up records
Cleaning and pest control records
Infection and infestation log
Outbreak notifications
Staff training and competency records
QA quarterly review minutes

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and Secure Information Management
policies.applies_to: All staff, contractors, volunteers, governing body members and the Administrator; all paper and electronic records
policies.purpose: To keep resident information secure, organized and confidential, whether on paper or electronically, while allowing residents, guardians and the Department to see the records they are entitled to see.
policies.policy: This policy meets 82-13-1-.05(8)(n) [first] (proposed), 'Procedures that support secure, organized and confidential management of information, including electronic records if applicable, that addresses state and federal confidentiality laws and regulations.' [AGENCY NAME] follows the HIPAA Privacy Rule as a health care provider, including the use and disclosure rules in 45 CFR 164.502 and the administrative requirements in 45 CFR 164.530 (privacy official, training, safeguards, complaints and sanctions). The agency keeps an individual file for each resident. The file is confidential and is available to the resident, the guardian and the Department (C11). Residents may see and obtain copies of their own records (C15). Confidentiality breaches are a monitored quality risk area (C35, QA-01). HIPAA is covered at staff orientation (STF-04). Resident information is shared only as allowed by law or with valid written authorization, and only the minimum needed for the purpose.

definitions.definition: Any individually identifiable information about a resident's health, care, payment or identity, in any form, including verbal, paper and electronic.
The single organized, confidential record kept for each resident, including the ISP, assessments, health information, consents and daily documentation (REC-01).
The least amount of PHI needed to do the task, applied to uses and requests other than treatment.
An unauthorized acquisition, access, use or disclosure of PHI that compromises its privacy or security, as defined by HIPAA.
The person named to develop and enforce privacy practices and receive privacy complaints: [PRIVACY OFFICER NAME].

procedures: The governing body designates a privacy officer ([PRIVACY OFFICER NAME]) and a contact for privacy complaints at [PHONE]. The Administrator posts the contact information in the staff area and includes it in the notice of privacy practices.

At orientation, before any contact with residents, every employee, contractor and volunteer receives HIPAA and confidentiality training and signs a confidentiality statement. Staff repeat the training each year, and the records go in the personnel file (STF-04, STF-06).
The agency gives each resident, and the representative, a notice of privacy practices at admission in an accessible format (RGT-05) and records that it was given.

Each resident has one individual file kept in a locked cabinet or in a secure electronic record, organized under standard sections set by the Administrator. Paper files are never left unattended in common areas, vehicles or open rooms.

Staff access resident information only when needed for their job. Staff use the minimum necessary information. Staff do not discuss residents where others can overhear, including in the kitchen, in the community and on the telephone. Staff do not discuss a resident with other residents.

Electronic records require a unique user ID and strong password for each user, with passwords not shared. The agency uses automatic screen lock, encryption of laptops, phones and portable media that hold PHI, up-to-date antivirus and operating system software, and regular backups kept secure. The Administrator removes access the day an employee leaves.

Staff do not send PHI by personal email, text, messaging apps or social media. PHI may be sent only through the secure methods approved by the Administrator. Staff do not take photos or video of residents on personal devices, and do not post anything about residents on social media (STF-07).

Fax, mail and email containing PHI show the correct recipient and carry a confidentiality notice. Staff verify the recipient's number or address before sending. Staff report a misdirected message to the privacy officer the same day.

Before releasing PHI to anyone outside treatment, payment and operations, staff obtain a signed authorization from the resident or legal representative. Exceptions are disclosures that the law permits or requires without authorization, such as reports of abuse, neglect or exploitation (ABE-01), reports to DBHDD and the state, and disclosures to the Department for oversight. The privacy officer approves any other disclosure.

Residents have the right to see and get copies of their own records (RGT-01). When a resident or representative asks, staff note the date of the request, confirm identity, and give access or a copy within [NUMBER] business days. A written denial is given only for reasons the law allows, with an explanation and the resident's rights to review. No fee is charged beyond what the law allows.

The guardian or legal representative and the Department have access to the individual file. DBHDD staff and state and federal reviewers get full access during surveys and reviews (GOV-02). Staff record each outside access request in the access log.

Residents' health information is not given to family members, friends or the media unless the resident, or the legal representative where one acts, has agreed in writing. Staff protect the resident's choice about who may know about his or her care.

Personnel files, resident files and financial records are stored separately. Resident files are never stored in the personnel file. Access to personnel files is limited to the Administrator, designee and authorized reviewers (STF-06).

Records are kept for the retention periods in REC-01 and then destroyed by shredding or secure electronic deletion. Staff do not throw PHI in regular trash. Equipment is wiped or destroyed before disposal. Destruction is logged.

Any employee who suspects or learns of a breach, lost record, lost device or wrong disclosure reports it to the privacy officer immediately, and no later than the end of the shift. The privacy officer records the report, contains the problem, evaluates the risk, and makes the notifications that HIPAA and other law require. The privacy officer also tells the resident and the representative and records what was done.

Staff who violate this policy face corrective action under STF-07, up to termination. The agency does not retaliate against anyone who reports a violation or files a privacy complaint (RGT-02, 45 CFR 164.530).

The privacy officer tracks breaches and near-misses, and the QA committee reviews them at least quarterly, as confidentiality breaches are a monitored risk area. The committee records corrective actions and retraining (QA-01).
The privacy officer reviews this policy and the electronic safeguards at least annually and whenever a system, vendor or law changes (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Designates the privacy officer and supports this policy.
Oversees privacy practices, approves disclosures, investigates breaches and tracks complaints.
Secures files and systems, controls access, ensures training and responds to access requests.
Protect PHI, use the minimum necessary, report breaches immediately and follow technology rules.
Gives the notice of privacy practices and helps residents exercise record access rights.

documentation: Privacy officer designation
Staff HIPAA training and signed confidentiality statements
Notice of privacy practices acknowledgment
Signed authorizations for release of information
Record access and copy requests and responses
Access log for outside reviewers and disclosures
Breach and privacy complaint log and notifications
Electronic access control and backup records
Record destruction log
QA quarterly confidentiality review

policies.title: Written Emergency Plan
policies.applies_to: All employees, the administrator, the responsible staff person, and every residence operated by [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure every residence has a written plan, known to all staff, for responding to emergencies so that residents are protected, evacuated, cared for and accounted for.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a written emergency plan for each residence. The plan sets out our strategy for responding to six emergency situations: (1) medical emergencies; (2) local and widespread weather emergencies and natural disasters such as tornadoes, hurricanes, earthquakes, ice or snow storms and floods; (3) manmade disasters such as acts of terrorism and hazardous materials spills; (4) unanticipated interruption of utilities (water, gas or electricity), whether in the home or across a local or widespread area; (5) fire, explosion or other physical damage to the residence; and (6) elopement of a resident, which is handled under EMG-02 (Mattie's Call Act, report to local law enforcement within 30 minutes). The plan is kept in each residence where all staff can find it. Staff are trained on it at orientation and at least annually. The home keeps a 3-day supply of non-perishable food and 1 gallon of water per person per day, and staffing is arranged so that all residents can be evacuated within 3 minutes. This policy meets Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 82-13-1-.05(8)(n)1-6 (proposed) ('.05(8)(n) [second]'), including item 1 (medical emergencies) and item 4 (utilities). It also meets 290-9-37-.07(6) (the written emergency plan requirement) and .07(6)(a) (weather and natural disasters), .07(6)(b) (manmade disasters), .07(6)(c) (utility interruption) and .07(6)(d) (fire, explosion or physical damage). Elopement (.07(6)(e) and .05(8)(n)6) is addressed in EMG-02, and fire evacuation and drills in EMG-03.

definitions.definition: The written, residence-specific document describing how staff will respond to each emergency type, who does what, whom to call and how residents are kept safe and accounted for.
Keeping residents inside the residence, in the safest area, during an emergency when leaving would be more dangerous than staying.

The 3-day non-perishable food supply, 1 gallon of water per person per day, first-aid supplies, flashlights and batteries, resident medications and the emergency contact and resident information binder.
The staff member designated under RSP-01 to act for the administrator and direct the response when the administrator is absent.

procedures: The administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) writes a residence-specific emergency plan before the license application is submitted and before any resident is admitted. The plan has a separate section for each of the six emergency situations listed in this policy.

The plan lists the residence address, [PHONE] for the administrator and responsible staff person, 911, the local law-enforcement non-emergency number, utility company emergency numbers, the poison control number, the nearest hospital, the local emergency management agency, and each resident's representative or guardian contact.

Medical emergency section: staff call 911 for any life-threatening condition, begin first aid or BCLS within their training, send current medication and health information with the resident, notify the representative or guardian and the administrator, and document the event under HLT-03 and ABE-02.

Weather and natural disaster section: the plan identifies the safest interior shelter area for tornado, the plan for flood and hurricane evacuation (primary route, alternate route and destination), and actions for ice or snow storms and earthquakes. Staff monitor weather alerts when a watch or warning is issued for the county.

Manmade disaster section: the plan sets out lockdown or shelter-in-place steps for threats of violence or terrorism, and evacuation or shelter steps for hazardous materials spills, following instructions from emergency responders.

Utility interruption section: the plan lists actions for loss of water, gas or electricity. Actions include calling the utility, using stored water, protecting refrigerated food and medications that need refrigeration, keeping residents warm or cool (interior temperature is kept between 65 and 85 degrees F, and cooling is provided when it rises above 80 degrees F, so staff relocate residents if this cannot be maintained), and powering any medical support devices from backup sources.

Fire, explosion or physical damage section: the plan cross-references EMG-03 for alarm, evacuation and drills, and adds steps for relocating residents if the home becomes unsafe and for securing property and records.
Elopement section: the plan states that a missing resident is handled under EMG-02 and repeats the 30-minute reporting rule.

The plan identifies where residents will go if the home must be evacuated for an extended period, and how they will be transported. It also identifies how residents who use wheelchairs, have sensory impairments or cannot self-evacuate will be moved.
The administrator confirms that staffing at all hours allows evacuation of every resident within 3 minutes, and adjusts the coverage plan under STF-01 if it does not.

The administrator checks monthly that the 3-day non-perishable food supply and 1 gallon of water per person per day are on hand and within use-by dates, and records the check on the emergency supply log. Perishables are rotated.
Each new employee is trained on the plan during orientation, before working alone with residents (STF-04), and signs the training roster. All staff are retrained on the plan at least annually.
Residents are told about the plan in a way each can understand, and are included in practice drills as their ISP allows.
After every actual emergency or drill, the administrator holds a debrief within 7 days, records what worked and what did not, and corrects the plan.
The administrator reviews the plan at least annually and whenever the building, resident needs, staffing or local hazards change. The review is dated and signed.
Any emergency that results in injury, relocation, resident harm or a report to DBHDD is reported and investigated under ABE-02 and REC-02.

responsibilities.duty: Adopts the emergency plan and makes sure the resources (supplies, backup power, transportation) exist to carry it out.
Writes, reviews annually and updates the plan, trains staff, keeps supplies stocked and keeps drill and debrief records.
Directs the emergency response in the administrator's absence and makes the required calls.
Know the plan, carry out their assigned actions, protect and account for all residents, and document events.

documentation: Written emergency plan for each residence, with annual review signature and date
Staff training roster for emergency plan orientation and annual retraining
Monthly emergency supply log (food, water, first aid, flashlights)
Emergency or drill debrief reports and plan revisions
Incident reports for any actual emergency (ABE-02)

policies.title: Missing Person and Elopement (Mattie's Call)
policies.applies_to: All employees, the administrator and the responsible staff person
policies.purpose: To make sure that any resident who is missing is searched for immediately and reported to local law enforcement within 30 minutes of staff learning the resident is missing, as required by Georgia's Mattie's Call Act.
policies.policy: When any staff member has actual knowledge that a resident is missing from the residence or from staff supervision, staff begin an immediate search and report the resident missing to local law enforcement no later than 30 minutes after the time staff first learned the resident was missing. Staff do not wait to finish a search before calling. Staff then notify the resident's representative or guardian and the administrator and report the incident to DBHDD. The time staff learned of the absence and the time of the police report are both written down. The local law-enforcement number is posted in each residence. This policy meets 290-9-37-.07(6)(e) (reporting the elopement of a disabled person to local law enforcement within 30 minutes of actual knowledge) and 82-13-1-.05(8)(n)6 (proposed), item '.05(8)(n) [second]' as it applies to elopement under Georgia's Mattie's Call Act.

definitions.definition: A resident leaving the residence or the care of staff without staff knowledge or authorization, when that person is not able to leave safely, or whose whereabouts are unknown to staff.
The moment any staff member learns, by observation or being told, that a resident is missing. The 30-minute reporting clock starts at that moment.
The Georgia law requiring that the disappearance of a disabled person be reported to local law enforcement within 30 minutes of staff learning the person is missing.

A current photo, physical description, clothing, medical conditions, medications, communication needs, known destinations and representative or guardian contact for each resident, kept in a readily accessible place.

procedures: The administrator keeps a missing person packet for every resident, updated at admission, whenever appearance or health changes, and at least every 6 months. It is kept in a place staff can reach immediately without unlocking a records cabinet.
The local law-enforcement non-emergency and 911 numbers ([LOCAL LAW ENFORCEMENT PHONE]) are posted next to the telephone in each residence and in the emergency plan binder.
Any staff member who cannot account for a resident calls out to other staff on duty, checks the whole residence, yard, vehicles and nearby areas, and counts all residents.
The staff member notes the exact time the resident was found to be missing. This is the time of actual knowledge.

If the resident is not located quickly, and in all cases no later than 30 minutes after the time of actual knowledge, the staff member or responsible staff person calls local law enforcement (911) and reports the resident missing. Staff give the resident's name, description, clothing, medical needs, any medications needed, communication needs and last known location, and ask that a report be taken.
The staff member records the time of the police call, the name of the dispatcher or officer, and any report number.

While continuing the search, one staff member remains with the other residents so that they are supervised. If only one staff member is on duty, that person calls law enforcement and the administrator or responsible staff person first and does not leave other residents unattended without arranging coverage.
Staff call the administrator or the responsible staff person at [PHONE] immediately, who then comes to the residence or directs the search by phone.
Staff notify the resident's representative or guardian as soon as possible after law enforcement has been called, and keep them informed.
The administrator reports the incident to DBHDD in the manner and time frame set out in ABE-02 and REC-02, and notifies the resident's support coordinator or case manager.

When the resident is found, staff check the resident for injury, arrange medical care if needed under HLT-03, tell law enforcement and the representative or guardian, and document the time and condition at return.

Within 24 hours the staff on duty complete an incident report that includes the time of actual knowledge, the time of the police report, the search steps, the time and place found, any injury and who was notified.

The administrator reviews the incident within 3 business days, determines contributing factors (supervision level, door alarms, ISP supports, staffing), and makes changes. Where the ISP or observation level needs revision, the administrator convenes the team under PCS-01 and OBS-01.

The administrator conducts a tabletop elopement drill at least annually, and for new staff during orientation, using a scenario that tests the 30-minute reporting step. The drill is documented with the time it took to call and any gaps found.
Staff receive training on this policy at orientation and at least annually, and are tested on the 30-minute rule.

responsibilities.duty: Starts the search immediately and ensures law enforcement is called within 30 minutes of actual knowledge, without waiting for permission from a supervisor.
Directs the response, notifies the representative or guardian, reports to DBHDD, reviews the incident and corrects causes.
Maintains missing person packets, the posted telephone number, drills and training records.

documentation: Elopement incident report with the time staff learned of the absence and the time of the police report
Law-enforcement report number and name of the person contacted
Notification log for representative or guardian, administrator, DBHDD and support coordinator
Missing person packet for each resident, with update dates
Tabletop drill record and training roster

policies.title: Fire Safety, Evacuation Plan and Drills
policies.applies_to: All employees, the administrator, the responsible staff person and residents of every residence operated by [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To protect residents from fire and other hazards by maintaining working fire detection and extinguishing equipment, a clear written evacuation plan and regular drills so that every resident can reach safety quickly.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] has established procedures and mechanisms for alerting and caring for residents in an emergency and for evacuating them to safety. A written evacuation plan with clear instructions is available in each residence, and each residence has secondary exits. Fire drills are held monthly, at alternating times and on alternating shifts, with at least 2 drills per year during residents' sleeping hours, and every drill is documented. Each residence has AC-powered, interconnected smoke detectors with battery backup that can be heard with bedroom doors closed. Each residence has 5-lb ABC fire extinguishers that are checked monthly by staff and annually by a technician. Exterior door locks must open from the inside without a key. This policy meets 82-13-1-.10(24)(b) (proposed), covering emergency alerting and evacuation procedures and the evacuation plan available in each residence. It also meets 290-9-37-.07(6)(d), the written plan for fire, explosion or other physical damage to the residence.

definitions.definition: A written, posted floor plan with the primary and secondary exits marked, the assembly point, assigned staff duties and clear step-by-step instructions.
A fire drill held while residents are in bed, at a time the home designates as sleeping hours, to test response when residents are asleep.
A second way out of the residence, other than the main exit, that residents can use if the primary route is blocked.
A designated safe place outside the residence, away from the building, where staff gather and count all residents.

procedures: The administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) prepares an evacuation plan for each residence with floor sketch, primary and secondary exits for every bedroom, route arrows, the assembly point and clear written instructions, and posts it where staff and residents can see it. The plan is also kept in the emergency plan binder (EMG-01).

The plan assigns each staff member on each shift specific actions: sound the alarm, call 911, assist residents who need help, check rooms, close doors and take the resident roster and medications list to the assembly point.

Staffing on every shift is set so that all residents can be evacuated within 3 minutes (see EMG-01 and STF-01). Residents who need physical help, who use wheelchairs or who have sensory impairments have individual evacuation instructions in their ISP or health record.

The administrator confirms that each residence has AC-powered, interconnected smoke detectors with battery backup, installed so that an alarm can be heard in all sleeping areas with doors closed. Staff test detectors monthly and replace batteries as needed, and record this on the fire safety log.

Each residence has 5-lb ABC extinguishers in place. Staff check each extinguisher monthly (gauge, seal, access) and sign the tag or log. A qualified technician inspects each extinguisher annually, and the administrator keeps the annual inspection record.

Staff check monthly that all exterior doors open from the inside without a key, that no door requires a key or special knowledge to exit, and that exits and routes are unobstructed. Bedroom doors may close but may not have double-cylinder locks.

Staff hold a fire drill at least once every month. The administrator varies the time of day and the shift so all staff and all residents take part over the year. At least 2 drills each year take place during sleeping hours.

During each drill staff sound the alarm, move all residents to the assembly point by the primary route (and by the secondary exit in at least some drills), take a head count against the roster and time the evacuation.

Staff immediately record the drill: date, time, shift, whether during sleeping hours, who took part, the exit used, the evacuation time, any resident who needed extra help and problems noted. The staff member who led the drill signs the record.
If a drill takes longer than 3 minutes or reveals a problem, the administrator corrects the plan, staffing or equipment and repeats the drill within 14 days.

In a real fire, staff alert residents, get them out first, call 911 from outside, count residents at the assembly point and do not re-enter. Staff then notify the administrator, the representatives or guardians and DBHDD as required by ABE-02.

After any fire, explosion or other physical damage, the responsible staff person decides, with the fire department, whether residents can return. If not, residents are moved under EMG-01, and the administrator reports to DBHDD under REC-02.

Staff learn the evacuation plan, alarm and extinguisher use at orientation before working alone, and are retrained at least annually (STF-04). Residents are taught evacuation in a way they can understand.

The administrator reviews drill records, extinguisher and smoke detector logs each month and signs the review. The administrator keeps drill and inspection records available for DBHDD survey (GOV-02).

responsibilities.duty: Develops and posts the evacuation plan, schedules drills, keeps equipment and records current and corrects deficiencies.
Ensures drills and equipment checks are done on each shift in the administrator's absence.
Perform drills and checks, evacuate residents, document and report hazards immediately.
Provides funds for equipment, repair and annual extinguisher inspection.

documentation: Evacuation plan with floor sketch posted in each residence
Fire drill log (date, time, shift, sleeping-hours designation, evacuation time, participants, problems, signature)
Monthly smoke detector and extinguisher check log
Annual extinguisher technician inspection record
Monthly exit-door and route check record
Corrective action notes and repeat drill records

policies.title: Designation of the Responsible Staff Person
policies.applies_to: The administrator, designated responsible staff persons and all employees
policies.purpose: To make sure a qualified, trained staff member is always in charge and able to carry out the administrator's duties when the administrator is not present.
policies.policy: The administrator designates a qualified staff member as the responsible staff person to act on the administrator's behalf and to carry out the administrator's duties in the administrator's absence. A residence is never without a designated responsible staff person. Residents of the residence may not serve as the responsible staff person. The administrator must be at least 21 years old and every employee, including any responsible staff person, at least 18. A person may not be designated until all minimum training and documented competence are complete. The designation for each shift is recorded or posted. This policy meets 82-13-1-.05(8)(o) (proposed), the designation of the responsible staff person.

definitions.definition: The qualified employee designated in writing to act for the administrator and carry out the administrator's duties when the administrator is absent.
The person named in the license application by the governing body as responsible for day-to-day operation of the residence.

Meets the age, background check, registry check, TB screening, first aid and BCLS, training and competency requirements in STF-03, STF-04 and STF-05, and has been assessed by the administrator as able to perform the delegated duties.

procedures: The governing body names the administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]), who is at least 21 years old, in the license application and confirms the administrator's qualifications before appointment.

The administrator identifies employees who may serve as responsible staff person. Each must be at least 18, must not be a resident, and must have an eligible criminal background determination, a clear registry check, TB screening, current first aid and BCLS, and completed orientation and competency sign-off in the personnel file (STF-03, STF-04, STF-05, STF-06).

Before designating an employee, the administrator reviews the employee's personnel file and confirms in writing that every requirement is met. No one who still has training or competence items outstanding is designated, and no employee works alone with residents until those items are complete.

The administrator gives each designee a written designation that lists the duties delegated: supervising staff, making admission-related and emergency decisions within limits, making required notifications, directing emergency response, handling incidents and reporting. The designee signs it.

The administrator reviews the designee's duties with them and trains them on the emergency plan (EMG-01), elopement response (EMG-02), abuse and incident reporting (ABE-01, ABE-02), medication emergencies (MED-03) and the contact list.
For each shift, the schedule shows the name and [PHONE] number of the responsible staff person. The schedule is posted in the residence or recorded in the shift log, and is kept on file.

When the administrator is on the premises, the administrator is the person in charge. When the administrator is away, the designated responsible staff person is in charge, and staff on duty are told who that is at the start of the shift.

The administrator may be reached by [PHONE] at all times, and the responsible staff person contacts the administrator for any matter outside delegated authority, including any allegation of abuse, neglect or exploitation, death, serious injury or elopement.
A resident may never be designated, asked or allowed to act as the responsible staff person, to supervise other residents or to hold keys, medications or records in that role.

If no qualified responsible staff person is available for a shift, the administrator takes the role personally or arranges coverage by another qualified person before the shift starts and records it. Where this cannot be done, the administrator follows the coverage plan in STF-01.

The administrator reviews designations at least annually and whenever a designee leaves, is disciplined, or loses a required credential or training. The designation is revoked in writing right away if a designee is no longer qualified.
The administrator keeps designation records and shift assignments and makes them available at a DBHDD survey.

responsibilities.duty: Names a qualified administrator and supports the designation system.
Selects, verifies, trains and designates the responsible staff person, schedules coverage and revokes designations when needed.
Carries out delegated duties, makes required notifications and reports to the administrator.
Know who is in charge on each shift and follow the responsible staff person's lawful direction.

documentation: Written designation signed by the administrator and each responsible staff person
Administrator's verification checklist of qualifications for each designee
Shift schedule or log showing the responsible staff person for each shift
Training and competency records for designees in personnel files
Records of revoked or changed designations

policies.title: Governing Body and Administrator Responsibilities; Adoption of Policies
policies.applies_to: The governing body, the administrator and all employees
policies.purpose: To state who is responsible for compliance, to make sure the written policies required by Georgia rules are adopted before a license is issued, and to make sure they are followed.
policies.policy: The governing body of [AGENCY NAME] is responsible for compliance with the Official Code of Georgia Annotated and DBHDD rules and names the administrator in the license application. Before a license is issued, the governing body adopts written policies and procedures outlining the responsibilities of the governing body and of residents that ensure compliance with the rules, and [AGENCY NAME] follows them. No member of the governing body, no staff member and no family member of staff may serve as a resident's representative or guardian. No one may solicit or induce a resident to name staff as a beneficiary of a will, trust or life insurance. Gifts are investigated, and involuntary gifts are reported to law enforcement and the legal representative. No life insurance is taken on any resident. This policy meets 290-9-37-.07(1) (written policies and procedures outlining the responsibilities of the governing body and of residents before licensure) and 82-13-1-.05(6) (proposed) (written policies on governing body responsibilities before a license is issued). It also meets 82-13-1-.05(8) (proposed) (the required policies and procedures of the governing body, which are listed by item in Procedure 4 below, with the policy of this manual that meets each) and the content requirements of 290-9-37-.07(3).

definitions.definition: The owner or group of owners or directors of [AGENCY NAME] with legal authority and responsibility for the operation of the Community Living Arrangement.
The person named by the governing body in the license application who is responsible for daily operation and compliance. The administrator is at least 21 years old.
A person chosen by or for the resident under RGT-04 to help make decisions or act for the resident, who is not a governing body member, staff member or family member of staff.
Money or property given by a resident because of pressure, undue influence, lack of capacity or deception.

procedures: The governing body meets at least annually, and whenever there is a significant change, and records minutes. It names the administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) in the license application and notifies DBHDD of any change of administrator or significant change in the governing body as GOV-02 requires.

Before the license application is submitted and before any resident is admitted, the governing body reviews and adopts this Policy and Procedure Manual by signed, dated resolution. The resolution is kept with the minutes. Policies must exist before a license is issued.

The governing body directs the administrator to implement the policies, train staff on them and monitor compliance. The administrator reports compliance, incidents, survey results and QA findings to the governing body at least quarterly (QA-01, QA-02).

The governing body confirms that the manual covers each item in 82-13-1-.05(8) (proposed): (a) code of conduct signed annually (COC-01, COC-02); (b) scope of services (SCP-01); (c) no admission or retention of persons needing more care than can be provided (ADM-01); (d) rights (RGT-01 to RGT-05); (e) medication management including all four pathways (MED-01 to MED-04); (f) abuse, neglect, exploitation, incident, injury, change-in-condition and death reporting (ABE-01 to ABE-03, HLT-03); (g) medical support devices and restrictive interventions (RST-01, RST-02); (h) admissions, discharge, refunds and record transfer (ADS-01 to ADS-04, REC-01); (i) QA with an injury indicator (QA-01, QA-02); (j) staffing and training (STF-01 to STF-06); (k) levels of observation (OBS-01); (l) resident conduct (RAC-01); (m) infection control (INF-01); (n) confidentiality and the written emergency plan, including elopement reporting within 30 minutes (CONF-01, EMG-01 to EMG-03); and (o) the responsible staff person (RSP-01). The content items of 290-9-37-.07(3) (service description, no admission or retention beyond capability, rights, medication supervision, reporting and investigation, admissions, discharge and immediate transfer, refunds, cooperative living, QA) are met by the same policies, with cooperative living in ADS-05.

The governing body adopts the responsibilities of residents that ensure compliance with the rules (cooperative living expectations in ADS-05 and resident conduct in RAC-01), and each resident is told of them at admission (ADS-01).

The administrator ensures that each employee receives the manual or the relevant policies at orientation, signs that they have read and understood them, and receives training on those relevant to their duties (STF-04). Employees must follow the policies.

No governing body member, staff member or family member of staff may serve as the representative or guardian of any resident. At admission and annually, the administrator asks each governing body member and employee to sign a statement that they hold no such role, and checks resident records for compliance (RGT-04).

No governing body member or staff member may solicit, encourage or induce a resident, representative or guardian to name any staff member or the agency as a beneficiary of a will, trust or life insurance policy. Staff who are asked to accept such a designation refuse and report it to the administrator the same day.

The administrator opens an investigation into any gift offered by or received from a resident, and records the circumstances, value, resident's capacity and wishes, and whether anyone pressured the resident. The gift is returned if it is not freely given or is not allowed under COC-01 and STF-07.
If a gift appears to have been given involuntarily, the administrator reports it to law enforcement and to the resident's legal representative and, as required, under ABE-01.

No life insurance is purchased on any resident by [AGENCY NAME], its governing body or its employees. The administrator checks resident records at admission and annually for any such policy, and reports any found.
The administrator reviews compliance with the manual at least annually through the QA program, surveys and incident review, and brings proposed changes to the governing body for adoption (GOV-04).
The administrator keeps a current copy of the adopted manual, the governing body resolution and minutes at the residence and available to DBHDD surveyors (GOV-02).
The governing body keeps ownership and governing body disclosures current, and reports changes to DBHDD within the time frames in GOV-02.

responsibilities.duty: Accepts responsibility for compliance, names the administrator, adopts the policies before licensure, provides resources and reviews compliance reports.
