Implements and enforces the policies, trains staff, investigates gifts, monitors compliance and reports to the governing body.
Applies the policies in the administrator's absence.
Read, follow and are trained on the policies, refuse any gift solicitation or beneficiary designation, and report violations.
Follow the cooperative living expectations and home policies in ADS-05 and RAC-01, with the supports described in their ISP.

documentation: Governing body resolution adopting the manual, with date and signatures
Governing body minutes and quarterly compliance reports
Employee acknowledgment of policy review (personnel file)
Annual no-conflict statements for governing body members and employees
Gift investigation records and any law-enforcement or legal-representative reports
Policy-to-rule crosswalk showing every item in .05(8) and .07(3)

policies.title: Licensure, Surveys, Corrective Action Plans and Sanctions
policies.applies_to: The governing body, the administrator, the responsible staff person and all employees; residents as to their cooperation with surveys
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] operates only under a valid DBHDD license, keeps its license in good standing, cooperates with surveys, and responds on time to survey findings and sanctions.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] does not operate a Community Living Arrangement or serve any resident without a valid license (or provisional license where available) from DBHDD. The license is posted in the residence, is not transferable, covers one residence, and the licensed capacity never exceeds 4 residents. We cooperate fully with every announced or unannounced survey or investigation, and meet every deadline for corrective action plans, disputes, hearing requests and fees. This policy meets 290-9-37-.07(1), which requires written policies and procedures outlining the responsibilities of the governing body and of residents that ensure compliance with the rules. Under this policy, the governing body is responsible for licensure and for responding to surveys and sanctions, and residents are expected to be available and free to speak with surveyors as they choose.

definitions.definition: A written plan, due within 15 days of the written survey report, that tells DBHDD how and by when each cited violation will be corrected.
An announced or unannounced visit or investigation by DBHDD to review records, the premises, staff and residents.
An enforcement action by DBHDD, such as public reprimand, suspension, revocation, civil fine, prohibition of persons in management or control, or limiting or restricting the license.
DBHDD's written permission, on its form, to depart from a rule on a showing of undue hardship or equivalent protection, with conditions.

procedures: No resident is admitted, and no services requiring a license are offered, until the administrator has the original DBHDD license in hand. The governing body confirms this before the first admission (ADS-01).

Application: the administrator submits a complete application, with all attachments and fees, to DBHDD. Attachments include a floor sketch, full ownership disclosure, records and criminal checks for owners and employees, and proof of electrical, water, sewage and fire safety compliance, including the State Fire Marshal inspection report dated within 12 months of submission. An incomplete application is not acted on. DBHDD's initial review of a complete application can take up to 30 business days, so no admission date is set until the license is issued.

Fees: the application processing fee is $300 and the annual CLA fee is $350, due on the anniversary of the prior license (30 days from invoice). The initial license fee is stated as the same as the annual fee, but DBHDD's fee table lists $650, so the administrator confirms the initial amount and due date with DBHDD before payment. Fees are non-refundable. A late fee of $150 applies at 60 days, and DBHDD may revoke a license when annual fees remain unpaid 60 days after invoice. A follow-up visit costs $250. The administrator calendars every due date and keeps proof of payment. If the home is accredited by a DBHDD-approved body, the administrator claims the 25% discount.
The administrator posts the license in a place visible to residents and visitors and keeps a copy in the administrative file.

The license is invalid if the home ceases operation, relocates, changes more than 50% of its ownership, or has a significant change in its governing body. The governing body does not operate under the old license after any of those events and applies for a new license before continuing. The administrator notifies DBHDD in writing within 15 calendar days of any ownership change. A new application and $300 fee apply to a change of ownership, name change, relocation or service-level change requiring a site visit.

A provisional license of up to 6 months is available only to a former personal care home, and only with an acceptable CAP. If [AGENCY NAME] holds a provisional license, the administrator tracks its expiration date and completes all CAP items before it expires.

Surveys: DBHDD may survey or investigate with or without notice, and a license application or license is consent to entry. When surveyors arrive, the person in charge greets them, calls the administrator at [PHONE] at once, and does not delay entry. Staff produce requested records without unreasonable delay and make residents and staff available for interview. Staff and residents are never coached, discouraged from speaking or retaliated against (RGT-02).
The administrator keeps a copy of the most recent survey report at the residence and makes it available for inspection on request by any person.

CAP: within 15 days of receiving a written report of violations, the administrator submits a written CAP to DBHDD stating, for each violation, the corrective action, the person responsible and the completion date. If DBHDD finds the CAP unacceptable, the administrator revises and resubmits it. DBHDD may require an internal CAP as well. [AGENCY NAME] carries out the accepted CAP and keeps evidence of each correction.

Disputes: if the administrator disagrees with a finding, the administrator explains or disputes it in writing within 10 days, following the instructions DBHDD includes with the report. Where the dispute rule requires it, an acceptable CAP is submitted with the dispute, and the CAP deadline is not missed while a dispute is pending.

Sanctions: DBHDD may refuse an initial license, revoke a license, or impose sanctions. Fines may be up to $2,000 per violation per day, capped at $40,000 per survey, in categories Critical ($1,201-$2,000), High ($601-$1,200), Moderate ($300-$600) and Low (no fine). Public reprimands are posted for 90 days, and suspension or revocation notices must be posted. The administrator immediately sends any notice of intent to sanction to the governing body.

Hearing requests: any request for a hearing on a sanction must be in writing and received by DBHDD no later than 10 calendar days after receipt of the notice of intent to sanction. The administrator logs the date of receipt and sends the request, by a method that gives proof of delivery, within that time.

Emergency orders: if the Commissioner orders relocation of residents, a monitor for up to 10 days, or a prohibition or suspension of admissions because of imminent and substantial danger, the administrator complies at once, informs residents and representatives, and cooperates in safe relocation under ADS-02 and ADS-04.

Variances and waivers: if a rule causes undue hardship and equivalent protection can be shown, the administrator may request a variance or waiver on the DBHDD form. The home complies with the rule until a written grant is received and follows all its conditions. During a Governor-declared public health emergency, DBHDD may suspend certain requirements, and the administrator follows DBHDD's written instructions and keeps them on file.
The governing body reviews every survey report, CAP, sanction and fee status at its next meeting and the QA committee tracks the findings (QA-01, QA-02).

responsibilities.duty: Holds responsibility for licensure, funds fees and corrections, and decides on disputes and hearing requests.
Submits applications, pays fees on time, posts the license, hosts surveys, files the CAP, dispute and hearing requests on deadline and notifies DBHDD of ownership changes.
Receives surveyors, notifies the administrator and ensures records and staff are available.
Cooperate with surveyors, tell the truth and do not retaliate against anyone who speaks to surveyors.
May speak with surveyors and are asked to be available for interviews; no resident is required to speak.

documentation: Original DBHDD license (posted) and copy in the administrative file
License application, attachments and Fire Marshal report
Fee invoices, payment proofs and due-date calendar
Notices of ownership or governing body changes sent to DBHDD
Survey reports (available at the residence), CAPs, revisions and evidence of correction
Dispute letters, hearing requests and proof of delivery with dates
Variance or waiver requests and DBHDD's written responses
Sanction notices and public postings with posting dates

policies.title: Medicaid Compliance, Billing and Service Documentation
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Administrator, billing staff, nurses, Responsible Staff Persons, direct support staff and any contracted provider
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] bills only for services that were authorized, delivered and documented, and that every Community Residential Alternative (CRA) claim to DBHDD or the NOW/COMP Medicaid waivers can be supported by the resident's record.
policies.policy: This policy meets Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 290-9-37-.07(1) by setting out, in writing, the responsibilities of the governing body and of staff for compliance in billing, contracting and documentation. [AGENCY NAME] will not bill for any CRA service until it holds an executed, signed DBHDD contract and the resident has been referred by the Regional Field Office. Claims are submitted through Carelon Provider Connects against each person's approved ISP and authorization, and only for services actually delivered and documented. The Administrator is responsible for billing integrity, and the governing body reviews compliance at least quarterly. CRA services may be subcontracted only to Host Home Providers, as the DBHDD Provider Manual requires (C34). All nursing delivered under the CLA license must be covered by site-specific nursing enrollment and must meet the NOW/COMP Part II and III contracting requirements (C34). Supervisors sign off on service notes and timesheets, as the DBHDD Provider Manual requires (C33). [AGENCY NAME] gives DBHDD and state and federal reviewers full access to records and the home (C33). Services must be delivered in a way that meets the HCBS settings standards at 42 CFR 441.301(c).

definitions.definition: Community Residential Alternative: the residential service delivered in the CLA and funded by DBHDD state funds or the NOW/COMP waivers.
Individual Service Plan: the resident's person-centered plan. It is the basis for every authorized and billed service.
The Carelon/Georgia Collaborative ASO system through which DBHDD-funded claims, authorizations and enrollment are handled.
The monthly report DBHDD requires for individuals served without a prior authorization in IDDC.
Electronic visit verification, a federal requirement (42 USC 1396b(l)) that applies to certain Medicaid personal care and home health services.

procedures: Before the first resident is admitted, the Administrator confirms that DBHDD has issued the CLA license and that the DBHDD contract is fully executed and signed. No claim is submitted before then. The Administrator keeps copies of both in the compliance file.
The Administrator confirms that each resident was referred by the Regional Field Office, and files the referral and authorization or funding approval in the resident's record before billing begins.
The Administrator keeps current Carelon/Georgia Collaborative provider enrollment and DCH/GAMMIS Medicaid enrollment and revalidation. The billing designee tracks revalidation dates on a calendar.

The Administrator checks that each resident's ISP is current and matches the service and units authorized before any claim is submitted. If it does not match, the claim is held and the support coordinator is contacted.

Direct support staff complete a daily service note for each resident each shift, as described in PCS-01. Each note covers services delivered, the resident's response, and any incident, change in condition or refusal.
Staff keep the timesheet for each shift. The Responsible Staff Person or supervisor reviews and signs service notes and timesheets within [NUMBER OF] days of the shift and before billing.

The billing designee reconciles notes, timesheets, the monthly staff coverage plan and authorizations each month, before claims are submitted. Any gap in documentation means the affected service is not billed.
The billing designee submits claims through Carelon Provider Connects within the payer's filing limits. Each claim is tied to the resident's approved ISP and authorization.

For any individual served without a prior authorization in IDDC, the billing designee submits the monthly MIER by the 10th of the following month. The Administrator confirms completion and keeps proof of submission.

The Administrator asks DBHDD in writing whether EVV applies to CRA per diem services, and keeps the answer on file. If EVV applies, the Administrator puts the required system and staff training in place before billing those services.

The Administrator does not subcontract any CRA service except to a Host Home Provider. Before any such subcontract, the Administrator verifies the provider's DBHDD enrollment and keeps the written agreement on file.

The Administrator confirms that every nurse working under the CLA license is covered by site-specific nursing enrollment and meets the NOW/COMP Part II and III requirements, before the nurse starts (see HLT-01).

The Administrator reports on contracted providers to the governing body quarterly. The Administrator also reports to the Regional Field Office before the end of fiscal-year Q1 and Q3, as DBHDD requires of providers that use contracted providers.
The billing designee reviews remittances and denials monthly. The Administrator investigates each denial and any overpayment. Overpayments are repaid promptly and the cause is corrected.

Any staff member who believes a service was billed in error, or documentation was falsified, must report it to the Administrator or the governing body chair right away, without fear of retaliation (see COC-02). The Administrator investigates and corrects the claim within [NUMBER OF] business days.

The Administrator makes all records available on request to DBHDD, the ASO, and state and federal reviewers. The Administrator tracks the ASO Quality Review score and the corrective actions taken in response to it.

responsibilities.duty: Adopts this policy, reviews billing compliance and contracted-provider reports at least quarterly, and acts on findings.
Keeps the contract and enrollments, confirms authorizations before billing, supervises billing, and responds to reviewers.
Reconciles documentation, submits claims and the MIER on time, tracks denials and refunds overpayments.
Reviews and signs service notes and timesheets and checks that documentation is complete.
Write accurate, same-shift service notes and record time worked truthfully.

documentation: Executed DBHDD contract, CLA license and Medicaid/ASO enrollment records
Regional Field Office referral and authorizations
Claims, remittances, denial and refund logs
MIER submission confirmations
Supervisor-signed service notes and timesheets
Written DBHDD response on EVV applicability
Host Home Provider subcontracts and nursing enrollment records
Quarterly governing-body billing and contracted-provider reports

policies.title: Policy Review, Document Control, Insurance and Rule Monitoring
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Administrator and all staff who use or maintain the Policy & Procedure Manual
policies.purpose: To keep [AGENCY NAME]'s written policies current, controlled and consistent with the rules and provider manual in force, and to keep required insurance and regulator access in place.
policies.policy: This policy meets Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 290-9-37-.07(1) and 82-13-1-.05(6) (proposed), which require written policies and procedures outlining the responsibilities of the governing body so that the residence complies with the rules. The governing body, through the Administrator, will review every policy at least annually and whenever the DBHDD Provider Manual is updated each quarter or a final rule changes. Each policy is version-controlled, and retired versions are kept. Rule status: the proposed CLA rules (82-13-1) would replace Chapter 290-9-37 (C22) and set the minimum operating requirements for CLAs serving up to four adults with developmental disabilities (C1). As of the DBHDD rules page checked on 10/14/2026, 82-13-1 was listed only under proposed rules, and no adoption notice was found (C23). [AGENCY NAME] therefore treats 82-13-1 as not yet effective. The manual is written to meet both the rule currently in force and the proposed rule, and the Administrator will confirm status with DBHDD Legal (404.657.2282, legal@dbhdd.ga.gov) before relying on either. [AGENCY NAME] maintains general liability insurance naming DBHDD as certificate holder at $1 million per occurrence and $3 million aggregate, and gives DBHDD and state and federal reviewers full access (C33).

definitions.definition: Rule text published for comment but not yet adopted. It has no legal effect until DBHDD gives notice of adoption and an effective date.
A policy with a version number, effective date and approval signature, and a retained history of prior versions.
The party named on the insurance certificate who receives proof of coverage. For [AGENCY NAME], DBHDD is the certificate holder.

procedures: The Administrator keeps the Policy & Procedure Manual in a controlled master file. Each policy shows its ID, title, version number, effective date and approval date.
The governing body adopts the manual and each revision by recorded vote, and the minutes record the date and version. See GOV-01.

The Administrator sets an annual policy review calendar. Every policy is reviewed at least once each 12 months, and the review is documented with the reviewer's name, date and result (no change or revised).
Each quarter, within 30 days after DBHDD posts a new Provider Manual, the Administrator reads the changes and lists any that affect policy, forms or practice.
Within [NUMBER OF] days after each such review, the Administrator drafts revisions for affected policies and presents them to the governing body for approval.

Every month, the Administrator checks the DBHDD privacy, rules and regulations page and the licensure page for any adoption notice for 82-13-1 or other CLA rule changes. The check is logged with the date and result.

Until an adoption notice and effective date are confirmed, the Administrator treats 82-13-1 as proposed. The Administrator confirms status with DBHDD Legal (404.657.2282, legal@dbhdd.ga.gov) before the initial license application and again at each annual review. The answer is documented.

When a final rule is adopted, the Administrator compares it with the manual within [NUMBER OF] days. The governing body then approves revised policies before the effective date, or as soon as possible afterward, and staff are retrained.

When a policy changes, the Administrator replaces the working copy, marks the old version RETIRED with the retirement date, and files it in the retired-policy archive. Retired versions are kept for at least [NUMBER OF] years and are never destroyed while a survey, investigation or claim is open.

The Administrator tells staff of each policy change in writing and by training. Staff sign an acknowledgment, which goes in the personnel record (STF-06). Residents and representatives are told of any change that affects them.
The current manual is kept at the home in [LOCATION] and is available to staff at all times. It is available to DBHDD surveyors immediately on request.
The Administrator obtains general liability insurance of $1 million per occurrence and $3 million aggregate, names DBHDD as certificate holder, and files the certificate in the compliance file.
The Administrator diarizes the policy renewal date at least 60 days ahead. Each renewal is checked to ensure limits and the certificate holder are unchanged, and the new certificate is sent to DBHDD.

The Administrator gives DBHDD and state and federal reviewers full access to the home, records, staff and residents, and designates [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] or the Responsible Staff Person to escort them. Access is never refused or delayed.
The Administrator reports policy review status, rule-status checks and insurance status to the governing body at least quarterly. Findings feed the quality improvement program (QA-01).

responsibilities.duty: Adopts policies and revisions, reviews rule-status reports, and ensures insurance remains in force.
Maintains document control, runs the annual and quarterly reviews, monitors rule status, and holds insurance and certificates.
Makes sure only the current policy is used on shift and gives surveyors access in the Administrator's absence.
Read and follow current policies, sign acknowledgments of changes, and report outdated or unclear policies.

documentation: Controlled master manual with version history and retired-policy archive
Governing-body minutes adopting and revising policies
Annual review log and quarterly Provider Manual review notes
Monthly rule-status check log and records of contact with DBHDD Legal
Staff policy-change acknowledgments
Certificates of insurance naming DBHDD, with renewal tracking
Records of access granted to DBHDD and state and federal reviewers

policies.title: Person-Centered Planning, the ISP and Daily Documentation
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Responsible Staff Person, nurses, direct support staff and every resident and representative
policies.purpose: To describe the services [AGENCY NAME] provides and to make sure every service is planned in the resident's ISP, delivered as planned, and documented each day.
policies.policy: This policy meets Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 290-9-37-.07(3)(a), a description of the services the residence intends to provide. [AGENCY NAME] is a Community Living Arrangement that delivers CRA services to adults with developmental disabilities. Room, meals and services are matched to each resident's assessed needs, and an ISP is required for each resident (C11). The services provided are: (1) room and a safe, clean, accessible home; (2) three well-balanced meals each day, 7 days a week, with the last meal no earlier than 5:00 PM and snacks offered mid-afternoon and evening, and special diets as prescribed (C11, see HLT-04); (3) daily personal assistance and support as the ISP directs; (4) medication supervision or administration under the pathway chosen for each resident (C36, see MED-01); (5) health monitoring and coordination with the resident's physician and nurse (HLT-01 to HLT-03); (6) community integration and employment support (PCS-02); and (7) transportation as the ISP directs (ENV-02). Services follow the ISP. The ISP authorizes any restrictive intervention or device (see RST-01). Staff must be awake in the home during their scheduled shift and enough staff must be on duty to protect health, safety and welfare (C9, see STF-01). Daily service notes are signed by a supervisor (C33). Services are delivered consistent with 42 CFR 441.301(c).

definitions.definition: The Individual Service Plan, developed with the resident, representative and team, which lists the person's goals, preferences, needs, supports and any restrictions.
Health Risk Screening Tool: a health-risk assessment completed for the resident and reviewed and signed by the provider's nurse.
The daily record of services delivered to a resident, written by the staff who delivered them and signed by a supervisor.

procedures: Within [NUMBER OF] days of the referral, the Administrator obtains the current ISP and support documents from the Regional Field Office or support coordinator and files them in the resident's record.

Before or on the day of admission, the Responsible Staff Person and nurse read the ISP and write a short Resident Profile covering preferences, supports, health risks, diet, medication pathway and any restriction. Direct support staff must read and sign it before working with the resident.

The Administrator invites the resident, the representative, the support coordinator and others the resident chooses to every ISP meeting. [AGENCY NAME] helps with communication and transportation so the resident can take part (RGT-05).

The provider completes the HRST at least 90 days before each annual ISP date. The provider's nurse reviews it and signs it. The nurse sends the results to the support coordinator and uses them to update healthcare plans (HLT-01).

Staff deliver services as written in the ISP. If staff cannot deliver a service, they tell the Responsible Staff Person the same shift, and the reason and the alternative offered are written in the service note.

Any restrictive intervention or device may be used only if it is authorized in the ISP and meets RST-01 and RST-02. Staff must not use a restriction that is not in the ISP, except in an emergency as RST-01 allows.

Staff write a service note each shift for each resident. The note covers date and time, services provided, activities and community outings, meals eaten, the resident's mood and choices, refusals, health observations and incidents. Notes are written the same shift and signed by the staff member.

The Responsible Staff Person or supervisor reviews and signs service notes and timesheets within [NUMBER OF] days. Missing or unclear notes are returned to the writer for correction, with a dated, signed late entry (no erasing).
Staff keep meal records showing what was served at each meal and snack. Records are kept at least 30 days. The Responsible Staff Person checks them weekly against the menu and any prescribed diet.

Staff report any change in the resident's condition, behavior or preferences to the Responsible Staff Person the same shift. If the change may require an ISP revision, the Administrator asks the support coordinator for a team meeting within [NUMBER OF] days.
The Responsible Staff Person reviews each resident's ISP goals monthly using service notes. A written monthly summary of progress, barriers and requested changes is placed in the record.
The Administrator makes sure staff are not diverted from ISP services to do housekeeping, laundry or other duties that reduce resident support. Residents may do household tasks only as PCS-02 allows.
If a resident is ever left in the home without staff, the ISP must document assessed capacity to be independent (STF-01). If it does not, the home is never left unstaffed.
The nurse and Responsible Staff Person confirm each month that medication, treatment and diet orders in the record match what is written in the ISP and healthcare plan (MED-01, HLT-04).
Residents and representatives may see and get copies of their ISP and notes on request, within [NUMBER OF] business days, at no charge or at the cost stated in the admission agreement (REC-01).
Each quarter the Administrator samples service notes against the ISP and billing (GOV-03) and reports findings to the QA program (QA-01).

responsibilities.duty: Makes sure each resident has a current ISP, that services follow it, and that documentation is complete and audited.
Briefs staff on each ISP, reviews and signs service notes and timesheets, and reports ISP problems to the Administrator.
Reviews and signs each HRST and updates healthcare plans to match the ISP.
Deliver services as the ISP directs and document them accurately each shift.
Help develop the ISP and tell staff when services are not meeting the resident's needs or preferences.

documentation: Current ISP and Resident Profile
Signed HRST
Daily service notes with supervisor signature
Timesheets
Meal records (kept 30 days)
Monthly ISP progress summaries
ISP meeting invitations and attendance
Staff acknowledgments of reading each ISP and Resident Profile

policies.title: Community Integration and Employment Choice
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Responsible Staff Person, direct support staff, residents and representatives
policies.purpose: To describe the population served and the services available, and to explain how [AGENCY NAME] meets the needs and desires of residents, with community life, work and personal choice at the center of daily routines.
policies.policy: This policy meets Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 82-13-1-.05(8)(b) (proposed), which calls for a description of the scope of services, including the population served, the services available, and how the organization plans to address the needs and desires of those served. [AGENCY NAME] serves adults with developmental disabilities, in a home of no more than four residents, as described in SCP-01. Services available are described in PCS-01. [AGENCY NAME] addresses residents' needs and desires through the ISP and by honoring each resident's day-to-day choices. Residents choose their visitors, have access to a telephone, and set their own daily routines. These rights are non-waivable under the rights rule (C15). Community integration is a monitored risk area in the quality improvement program (C35). Staff are oriented on the HCBS Settings Rule at hire (C33, STF-04). Residents are not staff and may not be required to do staff tasks unless the ISP documents voluntary participation (C9 applies through STF-01). Employment is offered as a choice, not a requirement, and no resident is penalized for declining or leaving a job or activity. This policy is consistent with 42 CFR 441.301(c).

definitions.definition: Having real opportunities to live, work, shop, worship, socialize and take part in community life like people who do not have disabilities, as the resident chooses.
The federal standards at 42 CFR 441.301(c) for home and community-based settings, including choice, privacy, access to the community and control over daily life.
A resident's free choice, documented in the ISP, to help with a household or program task. It may be changed or withdrawn at any time.

procedures: At admission, and at least once a year, the Responsible Staff Person asks each resident about preferences for activities, work, faith, friends, hobbies, community places and daily schedule, in a way the resident understands (RGT-05). The answers are written in the record and shared with the ISP team.
The Administrator makes sure each ISP includes community integration and, where the resident wishes, employment goals. If the ISP is silent, staff ask the support coordinator to revisit it.

Staff offer and help residents take part in community activities of their choice at least [NUMBER OF] times each week. Outings are planned around the resident's interests, not staff convenience. Transportation follows ENV-02.

Residents choose when to get up, go to bed, eat (within the meal schedule in PCS-01), bathe, and spend free time. Staff may suggest, but do not impose, a schedule except for documented health and safety reasons set in the ISP.

Residents choose their visitors. Visiting times are those agreed with the resident, and the home does not limit visits for staff convenience (RGT-01). Any limit must come from the ISP and be consistent with the rights policy.

Residents have access to a telephone for private calls at reasonable times. Staff help residents who need support to place and answer calls. Mail and other communication are not opened or read without the resident's consent.

Staff help residents who wish to find or keep paid or volunteer work, including contacting vocational providers or support coordinators, arranging transportation, and adjusting household routines. No resident is required to work.

Residents may not be required to do staff tasks such as cleaning common areas, cooking for others, laundry for others or monitoring other residents. A resident may help in the home only if the ISP documents that the resident chose to do so. The resident may stop at any time without penalty.
New staff are oriented on the HCBS Settings Rule, the resident's right to choose, and the limits on staff control at orientation (STF-04). Annual refresher training covers the same topics.

The Responsible Staff Person reviews service notes monthly for evidence that each resident took part in community activities of choice. The Responsible Staff Person records reasons when participation is low and acts on them.

Any restriction on visitors, telephone access, routines, access to food or other choices must be justified by a documented assessed need, written in the ISP, and approved under RST-01. The Administrator reviews every such restriction at least every [NUMBER OF] months.
The Administrator reports on community integration (outings, work, visitors, restrictions) in the quarterly QA review (QA-01), as DBHDD lists community integration as a monitored risk area (C35).
Residents and representatives may complain about lack of choice or community access at any time through RGT-02, with no retaliation. Complaints are logged and trended.

Each year the Administrator asks residents and representatives, in a manner they understand, whether the home is meeting their needs and desires. The Administrator uses the results to adjust activities, staffing and schedules.

responsibilities.duty: Makes sure community integration and employment choice are built into services, staffing and budget, and reports on them in QA.
Asks residents about preferences, schedules activities, and reviews notes for participation.
Offer choices, support outings and communication, and never require residents to perform staff duties.
Tell the team what they want, and may accept or decline any activity.

documentation: Preference and interest records
ISP community integration and employment goals
Activity and outing logs and service notes
Documentation of any voluntary participation in household tasks in the ISP
Records of any approved restriction on choice, with review dates
Orientation and annual training records on the HCBS Settings Rule
Annual resident and representative feedback
Quarterly QA community integration report

policies.title: Nursing Oversight and Health Care Coordination
policies.applies_to: Administrator, nurses, Responsible Staff Person, behavior support professionals, direct support staff and contracted professionals
policies.purpose: To make sure qualified professional staff oversee the services, support, care and treatment [AGENCY NAME] provides, and that each resident's health care is planned and coordinated.
policies.policy: This policy meets Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 82-13-1-.05(8)(j)1 (proposed). It demonstrates that appropriate professional staff oversee the services, support, care and treatment provided, including reviewing clinical documentation, conducting assessments, developing behavior support plans, service plans, healthcare plans and other protocols, and implementing assessment, care and treatment activities as defined in professional practice acts. The staffing and training policy (j) is among the policies the governing body must adopt (C5). Professional staff act only within their license and the practice act that governs it. Direct support staff do not perform tasks that require a licensed professional. All nursing under the CLA license has site-specific nursing enrollment and meets the NOW/COMP Part II and III contracting requirements (C34). Each resident has an individualized healthcare plan under DBHDD Policies 02-266 and 02-807 (C36). The provider's nurse reviews and signs the HRST, which is completed at least 90 days before each annual ISP. The resident chooses their own physician. The agency's duties for medication management are in MED-01 to MED-04.

definitions.definition: A person whose license or certification, such as an RN, LPN, physician, psychologist or other licensed clinician, authorizes the clinical work described in this policy.
A written plan for a resident's health conditions and risks, prepared by a nurse under DBHDD Policies 02-266 and 02-807 and followed by all staff.
A written plan, prepared by a qualified professional, of positive strategies to support a resident whose behavior puts the resident or others at risk (RST-02).

procedures: The Administrator designates a licensed nurse as [NURSE NAME], with a Georgia license in good standing verified before hire (STF-03). The nurse's duties, hours and reporting line are written in a job description.

Before the nurse begins work, the Administrator confirms the site-specific nursing enrollment for this CLA and that the NOW/COMP Part II and III contracting requirements are met. The confirmation is filed in the compliance file (see GOV-03). If a nurse is contracted, the contract is kept on file.

Within [NUMBER OF] days of admission, and whenever there is a significant change, the nurse completes a health assessment of the resident. It covers diagnoses, medications, allergies, diet, mobility, swallowing, seizures, skin, behavior and health history.

The provider completes the HRST at least 90 days before each annual ISP. The nurse reviews it and approves it by signature. The nurse gives the results to the ISP team so the ISP can reflect the resident's health risks.

Based on the assessment and HRST, the nurse writes an individualized healthcare plan for each resident under DBHDD Policies 02-266 and 02-807, within [NUMBER OF] days of admission. The plan names the risks, the staff actions, the signs that need a call to the nurse or to 911, and the physician to contact.

The nurse reviews each healthcare plan at least every [NUMBER OF] months and after any hospitalization, emergency room visit, serious incident or change in condition (HLT-03). The nurse dates, signs and files each review.

The nurse reviews clinical documentation at least [NUMBER OF] times each month. This includes service notes, medication administration records (MARs), incident reports, vital signs and meal records. The nurse records the review and gives written direction to staff for any problems found.

The nurse trains staff on each resident's healthcare plan, on health signs to watch for, and on tasks they may lawfully do. No staff member works alone with a resident before training on that resident's plan is documented (STF-04, HLT-02).

The nurse directs and checks medication practices as described in MED-01 through MED-04. This includes reviewing orders, checking that orders were signed within the past year, and supporting an independent biennial medication-management assessment by a pharmacist or RN at the site, as DBHDD requires (C36).

Behavior support plans are developed only by a qualified professional, [BEHAVIOR PROFESSIONAL NAME OR CONTRACTOR]. The professional is credentialed for that work. Each plan follows RST-02, and any restriction is authorized in the ISP.

Each resident chooses their own physician, dentist and other providers. Staff do not require a resident to use a specific provider. Staff help schedule and arrange transport to appointments, and send the resident's medication list and health information to the provider with consent (CONF-01).

After each appointment, staff give the Responsible Staff Person the visit summary and any new orders the same day. The nurse reviews new orders within [NUMBER OF] business day(s), updates the MAR and healthcare plan, and tells staff of changes.

The nurse tells the Administrator about any health or safety concern, and the Administrator takes action within [NUMBER OF] business days. Concerns that suggest abuse, neglect or a reportable incident are handled under ABE-01 and ABE-02.

Any nursing task that is delegated to unlicensed staff is limited to what the nurse practice act and DBHDD rules allow. The nurse checks competency and keeps a written record of the delegation, and the nurse remains responsible for oversight.
The nurse reports quarterly to the Administrator and QA committee on health outcomes, falls, medication errors, hospitalizations and healthcare plan reviews (QA-01).

responsibilities.duty: Employs or contracts qualified professionals, confirms nursing enrollment, and makes sure oversight is carried out and documented.
Assesses residents, signs the HRST, writes and reviews healthcare plans, reviews clinical documentation, trains staff and oversees medication practices within the practice act.
Develops and monitors behavior support plans and trains staff on them.
Makes sure staff follow plans and reports health concerns to the nurse the same shift.
Follow healthcare plans and orders, perform only tasks they are trained and permitted to do, and report changes promptly.

documentation: Nurse license verification and job description
Site-specific nursing enrollment and contract records
Health assessments and signed HRSTs
Individualized healthcare plans with review dates
Nurse documentation review log and written directions to staff
Delegation and competency records
Behavior support plans and professional credentials
Appointment summaries and updated orders
Quarterly health outcome reports

policies.title: Health Monitoring, Seizures and Choking Risk
policies.applies_to: Administrator, nurses, Responsible Staff Person and all direct support staff
policies.purpose: To monitor each resident's health, to protect residents at risk of seizures or choking, and to set out the emergency procedures for a medication emergency.
policies.policy: This policy meets Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 82-13-1-.14(14)(c) (proposed): emergency procedures such as the employees to be notified, the local poison information center telephone number, the person responsible for decision making, and the physician, clinic, emergency room or comparable medical personnel to be contacted in the event of a medication emergency. In a medication emergency, staff call 911 when life is at risk, call the poison center, notify the people named in Procedure 12, and follow the resident's physician orders and healthcare plan. Emergency medications (epinephrine, seizure rescue medication, glucagon and naloxone) may be given by non-licensed staff who are trained and found competent (C14). Seizure and choking risks are addressed in each resident's individualized healthcare plan (C36). No staff member works alone with a resident before training on that resident's plan is documented. Any special diet or device requires a physician's order.

definitions.definition: An overdose, wrong-person or wrong-drug dose, suspected poisoning, severe allergic reaction, serious adverse reaction, or any medication-related event that threatens a resident's life or health.
A medication ordered by a physician to stop a prolonged or clustered seizure, given by the route and in the situation the order states.
A documented risk of airway blockage from food, liquid or objects, usually identified by a swallowing evaluation, the HRST or the nurse.

procedures: The nurse identifies each resident's seizure and choking risks at admission and updates them at least every [NUMBER OF] months and after any change. Risks are written into the individualized healthcare plan (HLT-01) and summarized on the Resident Profile (PCS-01).
The nurse trains each staff member on every resident's seizure and choking plan, and on this policy, before the staff member works alone. The trainer, date and staff signature are recorded (STF-04).

Staff who may give a seizure rescue medication, epinephrine, glucagon or naloxone are trained by a physician, physician extender, RN or pharmacist, and are tested for competency at least annually (MED-04). Only staff with current documented competency give these medications.

Staff check that the physician's order for every rescue or emergency medication is on file, signed within the past year (MED-01). They check that the medication is available, labeled, unexpired and stored where it can be reached quickly.

For a resident with seizures, staff follow the resident's plan. During a seizure staff note the time it begins, stay with the resident, protect the head, loosen tight clothing, turn the resident to the side when it is safe, and put nothing in the mouth. They give any rescue medication as ordered.

Staff call 911 at the point stated in the resident's plan or physician order. If none is written, staff call 911 and then the nurse. Staff record the time, length, description, medication given and the resident's recovery in the service note and incident report (ABE-02).

For a resident at choking risk, staff follow the healthcare plan and any physician or speech-language order on food texture, liquid consistency, positioning, pace, utensils and supervision. Staff are within sight of the resident during meals if the plan requires it. The home never serves food outside the resident's diet order (HLT-04).

If a resident chokes, staff give first aid they are trained in, call 911 immediately if the airway is blocked or the resident cannot breathe, and tell the nurse. Every choking event is written up as an incident, and the nurse reviews the plan within [NUMBER OF] business day(s).
Staff take vital signs, weights and other measurements as the healthcare plan or physician order requires, record them, and report abnormal results to the nurse the same shift (HLT-03).
The nurse reviews seizure logs, choking events, weights and health observations at least monthly. The nurse reports changes to the physician and updates the plan.

In a medication emergency, staff first make sure the resident is safe. If the resident is unresponsive, not breathing, having a severe allergic reaction or in serious distress, staff call 911, give emergency medication as ordered, and stay with the resident.

For suspected poisoning, overdose or a wrong drug or dose, staff call the poison center at 1-800-222-1222 (the national Poison Help line, which routes to the local poison information center) and follow its instructions. They keep the medication container and have it ready. Staff then notify, in this order, the nurse [NURSE PHONE], the Responsible Staff Person [PHONE], the Administrator [PHONE], the resident's physician [PHYSICIAN NAME AND PHONE], and the resident's representative or guardian.

Decision-making authority in a medication emergency: the nurse directs care until the resident's physician or emergency personnel take over. If the nurse cannot be reached, the Responsible Staff Person decides to call 911 or transport, and the Administrator is notified at once. The resident's representative or guardian is told as soon as it is safe to do so (RGT-04). Staff do not delay emergency care to reach anyone.

The preferred emergency room, clinic and physician are written on the posted emergency list with phone numbers: [HOSPITAL NAME AND PHONE], [CLINIC NAME AND PHONE]. The list is posted by the medication area and reviewed monthly. Each resident's allergy and medication list goes with the resident to the hospital (MED-03).

After any medication emergency, staff complete a medication error or incident report as MED-03 and ABE-02 require. The nurse notifies the prescriber, reviews the cause within [NUMBER OF] business day(s), and the Administrator decides on retraining or corrective action. Events are included in QA reporting (QA-01).

responsibilities.duty: Makes sure emergency medications, posted contact lists and training are in place, and reviews all medication emergencies.
Identifies risks, writes seizure and choking plans, trains staff, directs care in an emergency and notifies physicians.
Decides on 911 or transport when the nurse is not available, notifies the contacts and checks that emergency supplies are ready.
Know each resident's plan, give emergency medication only when trained and competent, call 911 as needed and document events.

documentation: Seizure and choking sections of healthcare plans and Resident Profiles
Physician orders for rescue and emergency medications, special diets and devices
Staff training and annual competency records
Seizure logs, choking event reports and vital sign records
Posted emergency contact list with poison center, physician, clinic and emergency room numbers
Medication error and incident reports
Monthly nurse review notes

policies.title: Change of Condition and Emergency Medical Care
policies.applies_to: All direct care staff, the Responsible Staff Person, the Administrator, the nurse, and all residents served at [AGENCY NAME] at [ADDRESS]
policies.purpose: To make sure that a resident who has a change in condition, an injury, an accident, a serious or unusual incident or a medical emergency gets care immediately, that the right people are notified, that DBHDD is informed in the form it requires, and that each event is documented and followed up.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will immediately obtain the care a resident needs when the resident's condition changes or an emergency occurs. We will immediately notify the resident's emergency contact, representative or guardian. The Administrator or designee will report to DBHDD in the form and electronic system DBHDD accepts, and will document a summary of the event with follow-up and notifications (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 82-13-1-.18 [proposed]; 82-13-1-.19 [proposed]). Death notifications and reporting follow ABE-03. This policy meets 290-9-37-.07(3)(e) and 82-13-1-.05(8)(f) (proposed), 'Procedures for reporting and investigating abuse, neglect, exploitation, incidents, accidents, injuries, and changes in a resident's condition, including death.' Reporting and investigation of abuse, neglect and exploitation are addressed in ABE-01. Incident and injury investigation is addressed in ABE-02. This policy covers the change-of-condition and emergency-care part of those items, and the three policies are read together. No staff member may delay emergency care to ask permission or to complete paperwork. If this policy conflicts with a DBHDD reporting requirement, the stricter requirement applies.

definitions.definition: Any new, sudden or noticeable change in a resident's physical, mental, behavioral or functional status. Examples: new or worsening symptoms, injury, fall, seizure, choking, refusal to eat or drink, a new pattern of behavior, a change in skin, breathing or alertness, or a medication reaction.

An event that threatens or harms a resident's health, safety or rights, or that DBHDD requires to be reported. It includes injuries, accidents, elopement, restraint use and other reportable incidents. The full list is in ABE-02 and DBHDD's reporting instructions.
A situation that is, or may be, life-threatening or likely to cause serious harm unless immediate care is given.
The person legally authorized to act for the resident, such as a guardian or health care agent, or a person the resident has chosen to receive notices.
A staff member the Administrator has named in writing to make reports to DBHDD in the Administrator's absence.

procedures: Any staff member who sees or learns of a change in condition, injury or emergency stays with the resident, makes the situation safe and checks responsiveness, breathing and bleeding.

For a life-threatening emergency (not breathing, no pulse, choking not relieved, seizure over 5 minutes or repeated, stroke signs, severe bleeding, unresponsiveness, suspected overdose), staff call 911 first. A staff member trained in first aid and BCLS/BLS (see STF-04) begins first aid or CPR within their training until EMS arrives.

For a non-life-threatening change in condition, staff call the resident's physician or the on-call nurse for direction right away and follow the instructions. Staff call 911 or arrange urgent transport if the provider cannot be reached promptly or advises it.

Staff stay with the resident and do not leave the home below required staffing (STF-01). If only one staff member is on duty and must go with the resident, the staff member calls the Responsible Staff Person or Administrator at [PHONE] immediately for coverage.
The staff member notifies the Responsible Staff Person (RSP-01) and the Administrator immediately, by phone, not by text or email alone.

Immediately, and in any case once the resident is safe, staff notify the resident's emergency contact, representative or guardian. They give what happened, the resident's current condition, where the resident is being taken and a call-back number. Staff record the time and the person reached. If no one answers, staff keep trying and leave a message, and the Administrator takes over the attempts.

Staff send the following with the resident to the hospital or provider: face sheet, current medication list and allergy list (MED-03), diagnoses, ISP communication and support summary, guardian or representative contact, and any advance directive on file. A staff member stays with the resident or follows as soon as coverage allows, so the resident is not alone in an unfamiliar setting. This applies particularly to a resident who has difficulty communicating.
The nurse (HLT-01) is told of every change in condition on the same day. The nurse assesses the resident, or directs a clinical follow-up, as the circumstances require.

The Administrator or designee decides the same day whether the event is an incident reportable to DBHDD. For each event that is reportable (ABE-02, REC-02), the Administrator or designee reports to DBHDD in the form and electronic system DBHDD specifies, within the timeframe DBHDD sets for that type of event. [AGENCY NAME]'s internal standard is that the Administrator is told right away, and the report is entered no later than the end of the same calendar day whenever the information is known. If DBHDD's timeframe is shorter, the shorter timeframe controls.

If the event involves suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation, the staff member also follows ABE-01 immediately. If the resident has died, staff follow ABE-03 for notification of next of kin, the physician, the representative or guardian, death-reporting statutes and DBHDD.
If the event involves a restraint, a restrictive intervention or a medication error, staff also follow RST-01 or MED-03, as applicable.

The staff member who witnessed or discovered the event completes an incident or change-of-condition report before the end of the shift. The report gives date, time, location, what was seen or heard, the resident's condition, actions taken, who was notified and when, and the outcome.

The Administrator reviews the report within one business day. The Administrator documents a summary with follow-up and notifications, identifies the cause where possible, and starts an investigation when ABE-02 requires one. The Administrator cooperates with any separate investigation DBHDD opens (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 82-13-1-.19 [proposed]).

Follow-up includes: confirming the resident's return and discharge instructions, updating orders and the medication record, informing every shift in writing or by verbal hand-off, arranging follow-up appointments, and asking the ISP team to revise the ISP if the resident's needs have changed (PCS-01). A significant or lasting change in needs is also reviewed under ADM-01 and ADS-02, in case the resident's needs now exceed what the home can safely provide.
The Administrator enters the event in the quality assurance incident log (QA-01) so it is counted in trend review, including the injury indicator.

Each staff member is trained at orientation and annually on this policy, including how to call 911 and how to reach the nurse, Responsible Staff Person and Administrator. Emergency numbers are posted at each phone and in the staff area (EMG-01).

responsibilities.duty: Respond immediately, obtain care, begin first aid or CPR when trained, notify the RSP and Administrator, notify the family or guardian when directed, and complete the report before end of shift.
Direct the on-site response, arrange coverage, make sure notifications are made and confirm that the report is complete.
Take clinical calls, assess the resident, guide follow-up care and update the health care plan.

Notify the emergency contact, representative or guardian if staff cannot, report to DBHDD in the required form and system, review each report, document follow-up and notifications, and cooperate with DBHDD investigations.
Review the incident summary and trends under QA-01 and QA-02.

documentation: Incident or change-of-condition report with times and notifications
DBHDD report confirmation (date, time, platform, report number)
Log of calls to the emergency contact, representative or guardian, physician and nurse
Hospital or provider discharge paperwork and updated orders
Administrator's follow-up summary
Updated health care plan or ISP revision, if made
QA incident log entry
Staff training record on this policy

policies.title: Food, Nutrition and Modified Diets
policies.applies_to: All residents, direct care staff, the nurse, the Responsible Staff Person and the Administrator at [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure every resident has safe, well-balanced meals that match personal preferences, culture and health needs, that prescribed diets are followed exactly, and that the home keeps an emergency food and water supply and the required meal records.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides room, meals and services that match each resident's needs (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 82-13-1-.11 [proposed]). We serve three well-balanced meals a day, seven days a week. The last meal is served no earlier than 5:00 PM. We offer snacks in the mid-afternoon and in the evening. We follow special diets as prescribed. We do not serve food past its use-by date. We keep a three-day supply of non-perishable food and one gallon of water per person per day, and we keep meal records for 30 days. This policy meets 82-13-1-.05(8)(b) (proposed), 'A description of the scope of services the residence intends to provide to include the population served, the services available, and how the organization plans to address the needs and desires of those served.' As it applies to food and nutrition: the population served is adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities, as described in SCP-01. The services available are meals, snacks, beverages, meal planning, diet modification, and help with eating, shopping and cooking. [AGENCY NAME] addresses the needs and desires of residents by building menus from resident input, honoring cultural, religious and personal food choices, following prescribed diets and ISP supports, and teaching and supporting residents to take part in meal planning and preparation to the degree they choose. The full scope of services is in SCP-01.

definitions.definition: A meal that includes foods from the major food groups (such as protein, grains, fruits, vegetables and dairy or equivalent), planned with the nurse or a dietitian as needed, and consistent with the resident's diet order.
A diet prescribed by a physician or other licensed practitioner, such as diabetic, low sodium, renal, allergen-free, or texture-modified or thickened-liquid diets.
The date on the label after which food must not be served.
A written record of the menu actually served at each meal and snack, including any substitutions.

procedures: At admission, the nurse (HLT-01) records each resident's diet order, food allergies, swallowing or choking risk (HLT-02), weight history and food preferences, including cultural and religious preferences. The same information goes into the ISP (PCS-01) and the kitchen diet list.

The Responsible Staff Person posts the diet list in the kitchen, out of public view. It names each resident, diet order, allergies and texture or liquid requirements. Staff check it before every meal.

Residents and staff plan menus together at least weekly, with each resident's choices recorded. Menus must be well balanced. The nurse or a dietitian reviews menus for residents on modified diets. Substitutions are allowed at any time on request, and the substitution is recorded.
Staff serve three meals a day, seven days a week. The last meal of the day is served no earlier than 5:00 PM. Staff offer snacks mid-afternoon and in the evening, and offer fluids throughout the day.

Staff follow every prescribed diet exactly. A staff member who is unsure of the diet order, texture or thickener stops and calls the nurse before serving. No diet is changed, started or stopped without a written order, unless an emergency makes immediate change necessary. In that case, staff notify the nurse at once for an order.

For residents with a choking or aspiration risk, staff follow the swallowing plan in HLT-02, including positioning, pacing, supervision during meals and food texture. Staff do not leave a resident at risk of choking alone while eating.

Staff encourage and support, but do not force, a resident to eat. If a resident refuses meals or drinks for more than one meal, shows weight change or has trouble eating, staff tell the nurse the same day (HLT-03).
Staff report food allergies and intolerances to the nurse. They flag them on the diet list and the medication record (MED-03).

Staff store, prepare and serve food safely: wash hands, keep food at safe temperatures, clean surfaces, keep raw and ready-to-eat foods apart, and follow infection control practices in INF-01. Staff check use-by dates weekly and discard any food past its date. They label and date opened and leftover food.

The Responsible Staff Person keeps on hand a supply of non-perishable food for three days for every resident in the home, and one gallon of water per person per day for three days. The supply is checked monthly for use-by dates, rotated, and restocked within 24 hours of any use. The supply is part of the emergency plan (EMG-01).

Staff record each meal and snack served on the meal record the same day. If a prescribed diet was served, the record shows it. The Administrator reviews meal records at least monthly. Meal records are kept for 30 days and are available to DBHDD surveyors.

Residents have access to food and drink in line with their rights (RGT-01). Staff may limit access only when a physician order or a rights-restriction process described in RST-01 and RGT-01 applies, and the limit is documented.
Residents are supported to take part in grocery shopping, meal preparation and clean-up, based on their interests and abilities and as written in the ISP. Staff teach and supervise kitchen safety.

The Administrator reviews resident satisfaction with food at least quarterly through resident meetings and individual conversations. The Administrator documents the feedback and menu changes made, and reports concerns to the QA program (QA-01).

responsibilities.duty: Check the diet list before each meal, prepare and serve meals as ordered, supervise meals as the care plan requires, record meals, and report problems to the nurse.
Record diet orders and allergies, review menus for modified diets, evaluate nutrition and swallowing problems, and train staff on diets.
Post diet lists, check food supplies and use-by dates, keep the three-day food and water reserve, and make sure meal records are done.
Make sure the home has food, equipment and trained staff, review meal records monthly, and collect resident feedback.

documentation: Physician or practitioner diet orders
Kitchen diet list and allergy flags
Weekly menus and resident menu input
Meal records (kept 30 days)
Three-day food and water supply check log
Use-by date and refrigerator and freezer temperature logs
Nurse's nutrition and swallowing assessments
Resident feedback notes

policies.title: Residential Environment and Physical Plant Standards
policies.applies_to: All residences operated by [AGENCY NAME] under a DBHDD CLA license, including [ADDRESS], and all staff who live in, maintain or supervise the home
policies.purpose: To keep each home safe, clean, comfortable, accessible and homelike, to meet the physical plant standards in the CLA rules, and to make sure there are procedures for alerting and caring for residents in an emergency and evacuating them to safety.
policies.policy: Each [AGENCY NAME] residence will meet the CLA physical plant health and safety standards in Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 82-13-1-.10(1)-(27) [proposed] and the licensing requirements in 82-13-1-.06 [proposed]. Capacity will not exceed four residents. We hold one license per residence, and the license is posted. Bedrooms provide at least 80 square feet of usable floor space per person (not counting a built-in closet), no more than two residents per bedroom, at least one window, and closable doors, with no double-cylinder locks. There is at least one toilet, lavatory and shower for every four residents. Interior temperature is kept between 65 and 85 degrees F, with cooling provided when it is above 80 degrees F. Hot water at taps used by residents does not exceed 120 degrees F. The home has AC-powered interconnected smoke detectors with battery backup that can be heard with doors closed. Exterior door locks open from inside without a key. 5-lb ABC extinguishers are checked monthly by staff and annually by a technician. The home has first-aid supplies. This policy meets 82-13-1-.10(24)(b) (proposed; first two sentences): 'There shall be established procedures and mechanisms for alerting and caring for residents in case of emergencies and for evacuating them to safety. An evacuation plan with clear instructions shall be available within each residence.' Those procedures and the evacuation plan are in the steps below, in EMG-01 and in EMG-03. The home complies with the Americans with Disabilities Act and makes reasonable modifications for residents with disabilities. The standards are drawn from a proposed rule. If the final adopted text differs, [AGENCY NAME] will update this policy under GOV-04 and follow the final text.

definitions.definition: Floor area of a bedroom that residents can use, not counting a built-in closet.
A lock that needs a key to open from both sides. It is not allowed on bedroom doors.
A written plan with clear instructions, kept in the residence, for alerting residents and getting them to safety, with primary and secondary exits and the assistance each resident needs.
AC-powered smoke detectors wired so that all sound when one detects smoke, with battery backup.

procedures: Before the home is first occupied, and before any relocation, the Administrator confirms that the home has a valid DBHDD CLA license and meets the proof requirements for electrical, water, sewage and fire safety compliance (82-13-1-.06 [proposed]). The Administrator posts the license in a visible place in the home. The license is not transferable. The Administrator notifies DBHDD within 15 calendar days of any ownership change and understands that a license is invalid on relocation or cessation of operations. The Administrator does not exceed four residents.

Before admission, the Administrator measures each bedroom and records the usable floor space. Each bedroom must have at least 80 square feet of usable floor space per person (not counting a built-in closet). No more than two residents may share a bedroom, and a resident is not placed in a shared room without that resident's informed choice (RGT-01). The room needs at least one window and closable doors, and may not have a double-cylinder lock.
The Administrator confirms the home has at least one toilet, one lavatory and one shower for every four residents. Bathrooms offer privacy and have fixtures and grab bars suited to residents' needs.

Staff check the thermostat at least daily. Interior temperature is kept between 65 and 85 degrees F. If temperature rises above 80 degrees F, staff turn on cooling. If the home cannot be kept in range, the Responsible Staff Person calls the Administrator and arranges repairs, or moves residents, as needed, and treats the event as a reportable concern if required by ABE-02.

Maintenance checks water temperature at each tap used by residents at least monthly with a thermometer, and records it. The temperature may not exceed 120 degrees F. Any reading above 120 degrees F is corrected right away. The Responsible Staff Person limits use of that tap until it is fixed.

Staff test smoke detectors monthly and replace batteries as needed. The Administrator confirms the detectors are AC-powered, interconnected, backed by batteries and audible in every bedroom with doors closed. A faulty detector is replaced the same day.

Staff inspect each 5-lb ABC fire extinguisher monthly and initial the tag or log. A licensed technician inspects each extinguisher annually, and the tag or certificate is kept on file. The extinguishers are placed where staff know the locations and can reach them quickly.
Fire drills are held monthly, with at least two a year during sleeping hours. Each drill is documented (EMG-03). The Administrator reviews each drill and corrects any problem found.

Staff test every exterior door lock monthly. Each must open from the inside without a key. The Responsible Staff Person removes any lock requiring a key from the inside (an alarm used as a restriction is an RST-01 matter).

The evacuation plan with clear instructions is posted or kept in a known place in every residence (82-13-1-.10(24)(b) [proposed]). It shows primary and secondary exits and the assistance each resident needs. It is explained to residents in a form they understand and is reviewed with all staff at orientation (STF-04) and when the plan changes. The procedures for alerting and caring for residents in an emergency (EMG-01) and for evacuating them to safety (EMG-03) are kept with the plan.

At each shift start, staff walk the home to find hazards: blocked exits or hallways, loose cords, spills, broken furniture, and missing or damaged detectors. Staff correct hazards right away or report them to the Responsible Staff Person.
The home keeps first-aid supplies in an accessible, known place. The Responsible Staff Person checks and restocks the supplies monthly.

The Administrator inspects the home at least monthly using a written checklist covering the items above and the other standards in 82-13-1-.10(1)-(27) [proposed], including cleanliness, pest control, lighting, ventilation, safe storage of chemicals and medications (MED-04), and safe, working appliances. The Administrator writes repair work orders with a completion date. Urgent safety repairs are done within 24 hours.

The home is kept clean, in good repair and homelike. Residents may decorate their rooms and keep personal belongings as described in RGT-01 and RGT-03. The home is accessible to each resident, and the Administrator makes reasonable accommodations and modifications, such as ramps or grab bars, for residents with mobility or sensory disabilities.

The Administrator keeps the State Fire Marshal inspection report and other proof of electrical, water, sewage and fire safety compliance on file. The Administrator provides the file to DBHDD surveyors on request (GOV-02).

Before any change that affects the physical plant (renovation, relocation, change in room use or a change in bedroom assignments), the Administrator confirms the change meets this policy and notifies DBHDD as the license requires.

responsibilities.duty: Hold and post the license, keep capacity at four or fewer, confirm room sizes and fixtures, do monthly inspections, order repairs and keep compliance records.
Check temperature, water, exits and hazards daily, test devices, restock supplies and report problems.
Report hazards, keep exits clear, know the evacuation plan and take part in drills.
Provide funds for safe housing and repairs.

documentation: DBHDD CLA license (posted) and application materials, including floor sketch
State Fire Marshal report and proof of electrical, water and sewage compliance
Bedroom measurement record
Daily temperature log and monthly hot water log
Smoke detector and exterior door lock test log
Monthly extinguisher check log and annual technician certificate
Fire drill records (EMG-03)
Evacuation plan
Monthly environmental inspection checklist and repair work orders
First-aid supply check log

policies.title: Transportation and Vehicle Safety
policies.applies_to: All staff who drive residents or drive on [AGENCY NAME] business, all vehicles used to transport residents (owned, leased, personal or hired), and the Administrator
policies.purpose: To make sure residents are transported safely and with respect, that only qualified, verified staff drive, and that vehicles are safe, insured and maintained.
policies.policy: Only [AGENCY NAME] staff who have been verified under this policy may drive residents. Before a staff member drives, the Administrator checks the person's driver's license and obtains a motor vehicle record (MVR) check, which is also part of the personnel file (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 82-13-1-.08 [proposed]; DBHDD Provider Manual Part II, Sec. 1, Adequate and Competent Staff, E). [AGENCY NAME] carries business auto liability coverage that applies to owned, non-owned and hired vehicles. The Administrator will confirm the required limits with DBHDD and the contract and will not use any vehicle that is not covered. Vehicle incidents are reported as incidents under ABE-02. This policy meets 82-13-1-.05(8)(j)2 (proposed), 'Procedures for verifying licenses, credentials, experience and competence of staff.' As it applies to transportation, the procedures below verify the driver's license, MVR, credentials, experience and competence before staff drive, and again on a set schedule. The general credential verification procedure for all staff is in STF-03.

definitions.definition: Motor vehicle record, a report of a person's driving history and license status from the Georgia Department of Driver Services or the equivalent in the state of license.
A vehicle used for agency business that [AGENCY NAME] does not own, such as a staff member's personal car.
A vehicle rented or leased by [AGENCY NAME] for business use.
A staff member who has met every requirement of this policy and is listed by the Administrator as approved to drive residents.

procedures: Before offering a driving duty, the Administrator or designee verifies a staff member's credentials under STF-03, including a five-year employment history (DBHDD Provider Manual Part II, Sec. 1, E) and the criminal background and registry checks required before employment (82-13-1-.08 [proposed]).

For every staff member who may drive, the Administrator confirms that the person holds a valid driver's license of the correct class by examining the original license and copying it. The copy is dated and kept in the personnel file (STF-06).

Before the first drive, the Administrator obtains an MVR on the staff member and reviews it. The MVR is kept in the personnel file. Staff with a suspended or revoked license, a DUI or reckless driving conviction, or other violations [AGENCY NAME] has defined as disqualifying in writing, may not drive residents. The Administrator documents the decision and the reason.

The Administrator repeats the MVR check at least annually and whenever the Administrator learns of a violation, accident or license action. Staff must report to the Administrator within one business day any suspension, revocation, citation or accident involving a vehicle. The Administrator removes a driver from driving duties pending review.

The Administrator checks that the staff member has completed orientation and competency training that covers resident transportation: safe driving, loading and securing wheelchairs and equipment, resident supervision and behavior supports in a vehicle, emergency procedures and first aid (STF-04). A staff member does not drive residents alone before this training and the documented competence are complete. At least one staff member trained in BCLS/BLS and first aid should be present on trips when required to cover the shift (STF-01).
The Administrator maintains a list of authorized drivers, with the date of license verification and the last MVR date. Only people on the list may drive residents.

The Administrator keeps proof of business auto liability coverage for owned, non-owned and hired vehicles, with limits confirmed with DBHDD and the contract. The Administrator also keeps the general liability certificate naming DBHDD as certificate holder, as the provider manual requires (GOV-04). Staff may not use personal vehicles to transport residents unless the Administrator has verified in writing that coverage applies.

Each vehicle used for residents has current registration, tags and insurance card inside, a working seat belt for every seat, a first-aid kit, a fire extinguisher, a flashlight and an emergency contact list. Wheelchair-accessible vehicles have working lifts or ramps and securement devices.

Before each trip, the driver does a brief walk-around check (tires, lights, fluids, brakes, seat belts and lift) and records problems. Vehicles are serviced on the manufacturer's schedule. A vehicle with a safety defect is removed from service until repaired.

Drivers and passengers wear seat belts, and wheelchairs are secured, at all times. Drivers do not use phones by hand, do not drive impaired or drowsy, obey traffic laws, and never leave a resident unattended in a vehicle. Staff must meet the staffing ratios and supervision levels in OBS-01 and STF-01 on every outing.

Before leaving, staff review the resident's needs for the trip: medications that are due, seizure or choking precautions, behavior supports, toileting and communication needs. Staff carry the resident's emergency information and the emergency contact list. They take medications only as allowed in MED-01.

Residents' choices about community outings are respected (PCS-02). Transportation is arranged so that a resident can get to work, appointments, worship, shopping and social activities, within the resident's ISP.

If a vehicle accident, breakdown, injury, behavior emergency or missing resident occurs, the driver moves everyone to safety, calls 911 if anyone is hurt, and calls the Responsible Staff Person and Administrator at [PHONE]. The driver then follows HLT-03 and EMG-02 as applicable. Every vehicle accident or injury involving a resident is reported as an incident under ABE-02 and REC-02, and the Administrator reviews it and decides on any change to driver status.
The Administrator reviews transportation incidents each quarter in the quality program (QA-01), and takes corrective actions such as retraining or removing a driver.

Make sure only authorized drivers transport residents, check vehicles and supplies, and plan coverage for outings.
Maintain a valid license, report violations or accidents within one business day, follow safe driving rules and supervise residents.
Approve insurance coverage and fund vehicle maintenance.
