policies.title: Individual Records and Retention
policies.applies_to: All staff who create, use, store, send or dispose of resident records at [AGENCY NAME], in paper or electronic form, and the Administrator
policies.purpose: To make sure each resident has a complete, accurate and confidential individual file, that the file is available to those entitled to see it, that records are stored securely and kept for the required period, and that a full file moves with the resident on discharge or transfer.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps an individual file for each resident. The file is confidential and is available to the resident, the guardian and DBHDD (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 82-13-1-.11 [proposed]). On discharge or transfer, we provide the full file, in digital or paper form, to the receiving provider within 24 hours and document the reason, notifications and destination (82-13-1-.13 [proposed]). We keep meal records for 30 days, and quality assurance record reviews for 2 years (DBHDD Provider Manual Part II, Sec. 1, C). This policy meets 82-13-1-.05(8)(n) (proposed; the draft labels two consecutive items '(n)', and this is the first), 'Procedures that support secure, organized and confidential management of information, including electronic records if applicable, that addresses state and federal confidentiality laws and regulations.' This policy covers how records are organized, kept, accessed, secured and retained. CONF-01 is the companion policy covering privacy, HIPAA and electronic information security, and the two apply together. Federal documentation and retention requirements at 45 CFR 164.530(j) apply to [AGENCY NAME]'s privacy policies. Records of resident care are kept for the longest of the periods required by DBHDD (contract and provider manual), Medicaid and other payer requirements, and [AGENCY NAME]'s retention schedule of [RETENTION PERIOD, as confirmed with DBHDD]. Until the Administrator confirms the period in writing, no resident record is destroyed.

definitions.definition: The complete record of a resident, in paper or electronic form, containing the items listed in this policy.
Any resident information stored or sent in a computer system, an electronic health record, a cloud service, a DBHDD platform, email or a portable device.
Individually identifiable health information about a resident, in any form.

A person entitled to see a resident's record: the resident, the guardian or representative, staff with a need to know, DBHDD and other regulators, and anyone to whom the resident or representative has given written permission.

procedures: At admission, the Administrator opens an individual file for the resident and assigns it a file number. The file is organized with a standard table of contents, so any authorized reviewer can find items quickly.

The file contains, at least: the admission agreement (ADS-01); face sheet and emergency contacts; guardianship or representative documents; consents and releases (RGT-04); eligibility and referral records from DBHDD (ADM-01); the ISP and updates (PCS-01); health information, physician orders, allergies, medication record and nurse assessments (HLT-01, MED-01); diet orders (HLT-04); incident and change-of-condition reports (ABE-02, HLT-03); behavior support and restrictive intervention records when applicable (RST-01, RST-02); daily documentation and service notes; personal funds and property records (RGT-03); grievances (RGT-02); notices of rights; and discharge or transfer records (ADS-02).

Staff record entries at the time of the event or as soon after as possible. Entries are dated, timed and signed or electronically attributed. Staff never alter an entry. A correction is made by drawing one line through the error, writing the correct information, and dating and initialing it. Electronic corrections are made by addendum, with the audit trail preserved.

The file is available to the resident, the guardian or representative and DBHDD. A resident or representative who asks to see the file is shown it within [TIME FRAME] business days, with staff available to explain it in a form the resident understands (RGT-05). The Administrator logs every request. Copies are provided on request, and an authorized person who disagrees with an entry may add a statement.

Access to files is limited to staff who need them for their job duties. Paper files are kept in a locked cabinet or room in the home or the agency office. The key is held by the Administrator and the Responsible Staff Person. Daily-use records, such as the medication record and daily notes, are kept where needed for care and are secured when not in use.

Electronic records are protected with unique user IDs, passwords, automatic log-off, access limited by job role, encryption where available, and regular backups. Staff never share passwords. They never put resident information on personal devices or unapproved apps or send it by unsecured email or text. Staff follow CONF-01 for security measures, breach response and disclosures.

Records are not released to anyone other than an authorized person without the written authorization of the resident or representative, unless the law allows. Staff refer any outside request, subpoena or media call to the Administrator at [PHONE].

Records may be taken out of the home only when needed for care, such as taking a face sheet and medication list to a hospital (HLT-03), and the staff member keeps them secure and returns them. Staff do not leave records in a vehicle.

On discharge or transfer, the Administrator provides the full file, in digital or paper form, to the receiving provider within 24 hours (82-13-1-.13 [proposed]). The Administrator documents the reason for discharge, the notifications made and the resident's destination, and records the date and time the file was delivered, the method and the name of the person who received it. Medications, funds and belongings are handled under ADS-04. [AGENCY NAME] keeps a copy of the file after transfer, in accordance with this policy.

The Administrator retains the resident's file after discharge or death for the period set by [RETENTION PERIOD, as confirmed with the DBHDD contract or provider manual], which may not be shorter than the longest period applicable under DBHDD, Medicaid or other payer rules. Meal records are kept for 30 days. Quality assurance record reviews, at least 4 records or 5% of individuals each quarter (whichever is greater), are kept for 2 years (DBHDD Provider Manual Part II, Sec. 1, C). Privacy policies and HIPAA documentation are kept for at least six years from creation or the last effective date (45 CFR 164.530(j)).
Closed files are stored in a locked area, indexed by resident name and discharge date, and easy to retrieve for audits or requests.

At the end of the retention period, and only with the Administrator's written approval confirming that no audit, investigation, legal hold or request is pending, records are destroyed by shredding or secure electronic deletion. The Administrator keeps a log of destroyed records that shows the resident, the date and the method. The log does not contain PHI beyond what is needed.

The Administrator audits at least 4 resident files or 5% of residents (whichever is greater) each quarter for completeness, accuracy, timeliness and confidentiality (QA-01), and corrects deficiencies. Audit records are kept for 2 years.

All staff are trained on this policy and on CONF-01 at orientation, before they have contact with any record, and annually. Violations of confidentiality are reported to the Administrator, handled under CONF-01, and addressed through discipline (STF-07).
If the agency closes or changes ownership, the Administrator arranges for safe custody and continued access to resident records as required by DBHDD and informs DBHDD within the timeframes in GOV-02.

responsibilities.duty: Set up and oversee all files, confirm the retention period, control access, transfer files within 24 hours, approve destruction and audit files each quarter.
Write accurate, timely and signed entries, protect confidentiality and never share records improperly.
Keep health records, orders and assessments complete and current.
Make sure records stay secure at the home and that required entries are made each shift.

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
policies.applies_to: The Administrator, designees, the Responsible Staff Person, the nurse and all staff who identify or document reportable events or prepare reports for DBHDD, the Regional Field Office or the Board
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] reports every required event and data item to DBHDD and the Regional Field Office, accurately and on time, in the form and system DBHDD specifies, and keeps proof of each report.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will report all reportable incidents to DBHDD in the form and electronic system DBHDD specifies (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 82-13-1-.19 [proposed]). DBHDD may open a separate investigation of an incident, and we will cooperate fully. We will notify the RSA-DD within 2 hours of any death or high-visibility incident. We will submit the monthly MIER by the 10th for individuals without a prior authorization in IDDC. We will submit the quarterly quality management (QM) reports due October 16, January 17, April 17 and July 17. We will report on contracted providers to the Regional Field Office before the end of fiscal-year Q1 and Q3, and give the Board a quarterly report on contracted providers (DBHDD Provider Manual Part II, Sec. 1, Organizational Practices, A, B and C). This policy meets 290-9-37-.07(3)(e) and 82-13-1-.05(8)(f) (proposed), 'Procedures for reporting and investigating abuse, neglect, exploitation, incidents, accidents, injuries, and changes in a resident's condition, including death.' This policy is the state-reporting part of those items. It works with ABE-01 (abuse, neglect and exploitation), ABE-02 (incidents, accidents, injuries and investigations), ABE-03 (death) and HLT-03 (change in condition). If a DBHDD notice sets a shorter time or a different method than this policy, the DBHDD requirement controls. If a deadline falls on a weekend or holiday, we submit on the last business day before it unless DBHDD says otherwise.

definitions.definition: An event that must be reported to DBHDD under the CLA rules, the DBHDD provider manual or DBHDD incident instructions. It includes deaths, abuse, neglect and exploitation allegations, serious injuries, elopement, restraint use, and other events listed in ABE-02.

The DBHDD Regional Field Office contact for developmental disabilities, to whom deaths and high-visibility incidents must be reported within 2 hours. The name and contact details are kept in the reporting contact list ([RSA-DD NAME AND PHONE]).

An incident likely to draw media, public, legislative or law enforcement attention, or to affect the reputation of residents, [AGENCY NAME] or DBHDD, such as a serious injury, a missing resident, a crime or a major property event.
The monthly report that DBHDD requires for individuals who do not have a prior authorization in IDDC.
The DBHDD system in which prior authorizations for individuals are recorded.
The quarterly quality management report DBHDD requires from providers.

procedures: At orientation (STF-04) and each year, every staff member is trained to recognize reportable events and to tell the RSP and Administrator immediately. The list of reportable events (ABE-02) is posted in the staff area with the reporting contact list: [RSA-DD NAME AND PHONE], the Administrator's phone [PHONE], and the DBHDD reporting platform instructions.

The Administrator names in writing at least one designee who may make reports to DBHDD when the Administrator is unavailable. The designee has an active login to DBHDD's reporting platform. The Administrator checks the logins quarterly and removes access for staff who leave.
When a reportable event occurs, staff first obtain care and protect residents (HLT-03, ABE-01) and notify the RSP and the Administrator immediately.

For a death or high-visibility incident, the Administrator or designee notifies the RSA-DD by phone within 2 hours of learning of it. The caller records the date, time, person reached and information given. If the RSA-DD cannot be reached, the caller uses the DBHDD alternate contact and keeps trying until contact is made. Notifications to next of kin, the physician, the representative or guardian and others, and the death-reporting statutes, are handled under ABE-03.

For every reportable incident, the Administrator or designee enters the report in the form and electronic system DBHDD specifies, within the timeframe DBHDD sets for that event. The report is based on the facts known, and is updated when more is learned. [AGENCY NAME]'s internal standard is the same calendar day. The Administrator saves the confirmation, including the report number and date and time, in the incident file.
If DBHDD requires a different platform, or changes the form, the Administrator follows the new instructions from the effective date and updates this policy under GOV-04.

If DBHDD opens its own investigation, the Administrator cooperates fully, gives surveyors and investigators access to residents, staff and records (GOV-02), preserves evidence, and takes any protective action DBHDD requires. Retaliation against any employee who reports is prohibited (COC-02, RGT-02).

The Administrator conducts the agency's own investigation under ABE-02 and enters the outcome in the DBHDD system when asked. The Administrator also checks that follow-up and corrective actions are complete and documented.

By the 10th of each month, the Administrator submits the MIER for each individual who has no prior authorization in IDDC. The Administrator keeps a monthly calendar and a copy of each submission, with date and time, and checks the list of residents against IDDC before submitting.

By each quarterly due date (October 16, January 17, April 17 and July 17), the Administrator submits the QM report. Data comes from the QA program (QA-01, QA-02): incidents, complaints, rights violations, restrictive interventions, medication management, infection control, confidentiality breaches, ISP implementation and community integration. A report is complete only when the Administrator has checked the numbers against the underlying logs.

If the agency subcontracts any CRA services (permitted only to Host Home Providers) or uses contracted nursing or other professionals, the Administrator prepares a written quarterly report on contracted providers for the Board. The Administrator also submits the report on contracted providers to the Regional Field Office before the end of fiscal-year Q1 and Q3 (Provider Manual Part II, Sec. 1, B).

The Administrator keeps a state reporting calendar showing every due date and owner, and reviews it weekly. Two weeks before any due date the Administrator confirms that the data is on track. A missed or late report is documented with the reason and corrective action, and the Administrator tells the Regional Field Office if DBHDD requires it.
Reports contain only the information DBHDD requires and the minimum necessary PHI, and are sent only through DBHDD-approved secure channels (CONF-01, REC-01).

Copies of all reports, confirmations and DBHDD responses are kept in the incident or report file, and in the resident's file when the event concerns a resident (REC-01). Reports are retained at least as long as the resident record retention period.
The Governing Body reviews report timeliness and completeness each quarter (GOV-01, QA-02). The Administrator corrects any pattern of late or incomplete reports and retrains staff as needed.

responsibilities.duty: Recognize reportable events, tell the RSP and Administrator immediately and never delay or withhold a report.
Make all required notifications and reports on time, keep the calendar and confirmations, cooperate with DBHDD investigations and present reports to the Board.
Make reports to DBHDD in the Administrator's absence, using an active platform login.
Make sure the on-site response, immediate notifications and incident documentation are complete.
Provide clinical information for incident and QM reporting.
Review quarterly reports and contracted-provider reports and see that deadlines are met.

required_items.text: Prior to being issued a license, each residence shall develop written policies and procedures outlining the responsibilities of the governing body of the Community Living Arrangement and of the residents that ensure compliance with these rules.
A description of the services the residence intends to provide;
How the residence ensures that it does not admit or retain persons who require more care than the residence can provide;
How the residence guarantees the rights of residents;
How the residence supervises medications;
Procedures for reporting and investigating abuse, neglect, exploitation, incidents, accidents, injuries, and changes in a resident's condition, including death;
How the residence handles admissions;
Procedures for discharge and immediate transfers;
How refunds are handled when a resident is transferred, is discharged, or dies;
Expectations regarding cooperative living;

The quality assurance procedures that shall be used to maintain or improve the quality of care and services provided to the residents, including indicators of performance that shall be routinely measured and evaluated. At a minimum, the residence shall include as an indicator to be measured and improved, as necessary, any injury to a resident;
How the residence will ensure that staff are trained; and
How the residence handles acts committed by staff or residents that are inconsistent with policies of the residence.
Each residence shall have a written plan that effectively addresses the Community Living Arrangement's strategy for responding to the following emergency situations:
Local and widespread weather emergencies or natural disasters, such as tornadoes, hurricanes, earthquakes, ice or snow storms, or floods;
Manmade disasters such as acts of terrorism and hazardous materials spills;
Unanticipated interruption of service of utilities, including water, gas, or electricity, either within the facility or within a local or widespread area;
Fire, explosion, or other physical damage to the residence; and

Reporting the elopement of any disabled person from a Community Living Arrangement to local law enforcement within 30 minutes of the Community Living Arrangement staff receiving actual knowledge that such person is missing.

Prior to being issued a license, each residence shall develop written policies and procedures outlining the responsibilities of the governing body of the Community Living Arrangement that ensure compliance with these rules.
Required Policies and Procedures. The policies and procedures of the governing body shall include, but may not be limited to, the following:
A formal code of conduct communicating appropriate ethical and moral behavioral standards.
The code of conduct directly addresses issues such as appropriate use of resources, conflicts of interest, and use of due professional care.

The code of conduct makes it clear that under no circumstances will the following occur: (i) Abandonment of a resident; (ii) Threats (overt or implied) of harm or mistreatment of a resident; (iii) Corporal punishment of a resident; (iv) Fear-eliciting procedures directed toward a resident; (v) Any kind of abuse or neglect of a resident; (vi) Withholding basic nutrition or nutritional care from a resident; or (vii) Withholding from a resident any basic necessity such as clothing, shelter, rest or sleep.
The code of conduct provides a process for what employees must do if they become aware of unacceptable behavior.
The code of conduct is acknowledged by signature of all employees and contractors at least annually.
Appropriate disciplinary action is taken in response to departures from approved policies or violations of the code of conduct.

A description of the scope of services the residence intends to provide to include the population served, the services available, and how the organization plans to address the needs and desires of those served;
How the residence ensures that it does not admit or retain persons who require more care than the residence can provide, as outlined in Section .12 of these Rules.
How the residence guarantees the rights of the residents as outlined in Section .15 of these Rules.

Procedures for all aspects of medication management including but not limited to medication orders and procurement, storage, security, method(s) of administration used (proxy caregiver, licensed healthcare professional, assistance with self-administration or self-directed self-administration), documentation of all aspects of medication management, and disposal of discontinued or out of date medications as outlined in Section .14 of these Rules.
Procedures for reporting abuse, neglect, exploitation, incidents, accidents, injuries, and changes in a resident's condition, including death;

Procedures that outline and identify the medical support devices and other restrictive interventions that are implemented or prohibited by the organization and licensure requirements as outlined in Sections .16 and .17 of these Rules.
How the residence handles admissions and discharges, including:
Procedures for discharge/transfer/immediate transfer due to medical or behavioral needs of residents;
How refunds are handled when a resident is transferred, is discharged, or dies;
How the resident's complete record, unused special medical supplies, personal belongings, medications, funds and burial accounts are transferred when a resident is transferred or discharged.
Expectations regarding cooperative living.

The internal quality assurance procedures that shall be used to minimize risk and maintain or improve the quality of care and services provided to the residents, including processes for how deficiencies and risks are identified and managed on an ongoing basis. At a minimum, the residence shall include as an indicator to be measured and improved, as necessary, any injury to a resident;
What constitutes the staffing requirements and how the residence will ensure that staff are trained, including but not limited to the following required elements:

Policy demonstrates that appropriate professional staff oversee the services, support, care and treatment provided including reviewing clinical documentation, conducting assessments, developing behavior support plans, service plans, healthcare plans, and other protocols, and implementing assessment, care and treatment activities as defined in professional practice acts.
Procedures for verifying licenses, credentials, experience and competence of staff.
Personnel shall be assigned duties consistent with their position, training, and experience and with the requirements of Section .15 of these rules.
How the residence handles acts committed by staff that are inconsistent with policies of the residence.

required_items.text: Each residence shall have a written plan that effectively addresses the Community Living Arrangement's strategy for responding to the following emergency situations: 1. Medical emergencies; 2. Local and widespread weather emergencies or natural disasters, such as tornadoes, hurricanes, earthquakes, ice or snow storms, or floods; 3. Manmade disasters such as acts of terrorism and hazardous materials spills; 4. Unanticipated interruption of service utilities, including water, gas, or electricity, within the facility or within a local or widespread area; 5. Fire, explosion, or other physical damage to the residence; and 6. Reporting the elopement (Georgia's Mattie's Call Act) of any disabled person from a Community Living Arrangement to local law enforcement within 30 minutes of the Community Living Arrangement staff receiving actual knowledge that such person is missing.

The Community Living Arrangement administrator shall designate a qualified staff member as the responsible staff person to act on his or her behalf and to carry out his or her duties in the administrator's absence. Residents of the Community Living Arrangement may not serve as the responsible staff person.
Community Living Arrangements shall have a written policy that specifies the procedures to be followed regarding oversight of medication. Such policy shall include but may not be limited to:

Processes for determining the method(s) of medication administration that may be used for residents, including an assessment to determine the resident's capacity to self-administer medications, as applicable.
Actions to take when concerns regarding a resident's capacity to self-administer are identified.

Emergency procedures such as the employees to be notified, the local poison information center telephone number, the person responsible for decision making, and the physician, clinic, emergency room, or comparable medical personnel to be contacted in the event of a medication emergency;
Procedures regarding management of medications including disposal of discontinued or out-of-date medications;
Definitions and procedures for documenting and reporting medication errors;
Procedures to flag allergies and other critical information; and
Requirements for staff training.
Each admission agreement shall include a written procedure for handling discharge and transfer of the resident that complies with these rules.

All Community Living Arrangements must maintain a monthly plan for specific staff coverage in advance of the month, a record of actual staff coverage, and a plan for provision of all required services.

There shall be established procedures and mechanisms for alerting and caring for residents in case of emergencies and for evacuating them to safety. An evacuation plan with clear instructions shall be available within each residence.
The Community Living Arrangement shall have and enforce effective procedures to minimize to the greatest extent possible the use of restraints.

official.notes: No single policy checklist or review form exists for this program. The DBHDD CLA Application Packet (v. 1/1/2026) lists only application paperwork and contains no policy checklist. Policy content therefore comes from the regulation sections that list required written policies. (1) Rule 290-9-37-.07(1), (3) and (6) is the current codified rule, and the 2026 application packet still points applicants to it. (2) Proposed Rule 82-13-1-.05(8) expands that list. Its public notice describes it as the list of required governing-body policies and says the new chapter will amend 290-9-37. I could not verify adoption, so confirm the status on DBHDD's 'Privacy, Rules & Regulations' page before finalizing. The proposed text contains drafting glitches: two items are labeled '(n)', and some cross-references are off. The items are reproduced as drafted. Section references inside the proposed rule point to .12 (admission), .14 (medications), .15 (rights), .16 (medical support devices) and .17 (restraints), so those sections should be cross-referenced in the manual. Suggested organization: one manual with a table of contents and policies in the same order as .05(8)(a) through (o). Number each policy with the rule item it satisfies. Add a crosswalk to 290-9-37-.07(3)(a)-(l) and (6)(a)-(e) so a reviewer can find each item under either rule. Keep the emergency/disaster plan as its own section covering all required scenarios, including the 30-minute elopement reporting. The packet gives no policy-upload slot, but the rules require the policies to exist before a license is issued, and surveys (announced or unannounced) can require production of records. Surveys by DBHDD are described in proposed rule .07. After a survey report, a written corrective action plan is due within 15 days, and a dispute may be offered within 10 days. Submit the application online through the GAHLES portal (https://gahles.dch.georgia.gov/). Initial review takes 30 business days. Send questions to Licensure.Application@dbhdd.ga.gov. A separate license is required for each residence. Proposed capacity is no more than four residents. Because these sites deliver CRA services under DBHDD contracts and the NOW/COMP waivers, also check the DBHDD DD provider manuals and DBHDD policies for additional requirements. I did not extract those manuals' policy requirements. Personnel-file items, the training and background-check requirements (.08), and the admission agreement contents (.12(7)) are operational or record requirements in the proposed rule, not listed policy items. Address them in the staffing and admission policies.
